# Concept map

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts

A knowledge graph describes entities and the relationships between them. In Intuition, an **atom** represents an entity with exact data bytes, a **triple** expresses a directed relationship, and a **signal** is an economic position associated with an atom or triple.

## Identify the thing and its representation

A recording and an artist are different entities. Each can have a canonical Intuition Identifier (IID), but the protocol's atom ID identifies a particular byte representation. Equal atom data produces the same atom ID; different descriptive payloads can refer to the same IID while producing different atom IDs.

| Value | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| IID | Name an entity within an identifier scheme |
| Atom data | Persist the exact representation selected for that entity |
| Atom ID | Refer to that representation in triples and protocol operations |
| Companion context URIs | Publish discovery leads without changing the builder's atom data |
| Enrichment artifacts | Keep updatable descriptions and their provenance |

The [offline quickstart](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/get-started/quickstart) derives the golden ISRC fixture. It does not identify the synthetic recording used in the [music catalog](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/examples/music-catalog).

## State a relationship explicitly

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  recording["Recording atom: subject"] --> predicate["by artist atom: predicate"] --> artist["Artist atom: object"]
```

A triple is an ordered tuple of subject, predicate, and object IDs. “Recording **by artist** artist” differs from the reversed tuple. A relationship field in JSON or a Creation Profile suggestion does not create either triple; your application must build the edge explicitly.

The [predicate registry](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/predicates) separates the application key, such as `byArtist`, from its label, serialized atom data, and atom ID. Use that shared definition rather than constructing a predicate from a label alone. Changing identity-bearing predicate data can create a different predicate atom.

## Add meaning and evidence

A **classification** describes an entity type. A **Creation Profile** supplies its input fields, identity ladder, and suggested relationships. Parsing recognizes inputs; classification plugins interpret them; enrichment retrieves additional fields from configured providers. A provider plan is a list of capabilities, not fetched evidence.

Keep descriptions, provider provenance, and application state separate from stable identity wherever possible. A valid identifier establishes syntax and derivation rules, not the truth of every associated claim. See [creation forms](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/creation-profiles) and [classification and enrichment](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/classify-enrich).

## Understand signals and storage

Protocol vaults associate shares and assets with a term on a particular curve. Deposits and redemptions change positions. Your application decides how those positions affect curation, reputation, or ranking.

Locally building a term creates no persistent record. An on-chain write requires submission and a successful receipt; a Core node must separately ingest and project events before its indexed records are visible. [Query a Core node](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/query-core) for the V2 read path.

## Continue with the concept pages

- [Representation profiles](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/representation-profiles): choose bytes for an IID and keep companion metadata separate.
- [Protocol writes](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/protocol-writes): distinguish local plans, RPC reads, wallet submission, and indexed visibility.

Source: [Core package concepts](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/README.md#core-concepts).

# Protocol writes

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/protocol-writes

Applies to V2 · `@0xintuition/sdk` 4.0.0 · `@0xintuition/protocol` 4.0.0 · `@0xintuition/periphery` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/deployments` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/cli` 0.1.0

A protocol write changes on-chain state through a signed transaction. Building atom bytes or an action envelope can happen locally; reading a quote needs contract state; submission requires an authorized signer. A prepared request is not a transaction, a transaction hash is not a successful receipt, and a receipt does not prove a Core node has indexed the change.

**Builds on:** [Representation profiles](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/representation-profiles), deterministic IDs, vaults, and classifications.

**Implemented by:** [sdk](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/sdk), [protocol](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/protocol), [periphery](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/periphery), [deployments](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/deployments), [cli](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/cli).

## How it works

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant App
  participant SDK
  participant Wallet
  participant Chain
  participant Core
  App->>SDK: Exact bytes, IDs, receiver, amounts
  SDK->>Chain: Reads for quotes and readiness
  SDK-->>App: Plan and transaction requests
  App->>App: Human review and authorization
  App->>Wallet: Approved request
  Wallet->>Chain: Signed transaction
  Chain-->>App: Receipt or revert
  Chain->>Core: Events, when indexing is configured
  App->>Core: Query projected records
```

| Operation | Runtime boundary |
| --- | --- |
| Primitive builder, calldata encoder, client-free envelope | Local computation; envelope inputs include caller-supplied read context |
| SDK quote, readiness, or preparation action | May perform RPC reads; no submission merely because a plan is returned |
| Protocol write wrapper or `feeProxyExecutePlan` | Can simulate and submit using wallet clients |
| Receipt parsing | Confirms success or failure and filters expected contract events |
| Core query | Reads that node's projected state, which may lag chain confirmation |

A quote is a snapshot, not a reservation. Before signing, review the chain, deployment, calldata, value, receiver, required signer, minimum output, and ordered steps. Recheck stale state and deployment capabilities. [Contract artifacts](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/compatibility#contract-artifacts-and-deployments) describe an interface, not a guarantee that every deployment implements it.

FeeProxy plans can route creation and deposits and require different signers for approvals. `feeProxyExecutePlan` submits and waits for receipts; a later failure can leave earlier steps completed. Record those receipts and reread state before resuming. A refund helper can return `null` when nothing is claimable.

## Protocol writes - Example

This helper builds an ordinary descriptive atom and asks the SDK for a create-and-seed plan. **Calling it makes contract reads; it does not submit.** Its caller supplies a configured MultiVault, receiver, name, and amount in base units.

```ts
import { buildThing } from '@0xintuition/primitives';
import { multivaultCreateAndSeedTerm } from '@0xintuition/sdk/actions';
import type { WriteConfig } from '@0xintuition/protocol';
import { stringToHex, type Address } from 'viem';

export async function prepareNamedAtom(
  config: WriteConfig,
  receiver: Address,
  name: string,
  assetsIn: bigint,
) {
  const result = buildThing({ name });
  if (!result.success) throw new Error(result.errors.join('; '));
  return multivaultCreateAndSeedTerm(config, {
    receiver,
    atomsToCreate: [
      {
        termId: result.value.id,
        data: stringToHex(result.value.data),
        assetsIn,
      },
    ],
    seedDeposits: [],
  });
}
```

The caller must handle an existing atom and current creation costs. The same name and serialized data produce the same ID; deriving it does not reserve it. This ordinary creation plan does not register companion URIs. Use `multiVaultCreateAtomsWithUris` or a URI-aware FeeProxy preparation path when those entries must be registered, after reading live URI limits.

## Common mistakes

- Assuming a helper's name proves it submits: `multivaultCreateAndSeedTerm` returns a plan.
- Calling a write wrapper while intending only an offline preview.
- Treating a transaction hash as a receipt or a receipt as indexed visibility.
- Assuming a hook reset cancels a pending wallet request or transaction.
- Treating an off-chain Core API insert as on-chain registration.

## Next

[Build action plans and envelopes](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/action-plans) for review, then [query a Core node](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/query-core) to understand the separate read path. Its default source stack requires explicit indexing configuration before it ingests chain events.

Sources: [Action-plan ownership](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/sdk/docs/action-plans.md), [MultiVault actions](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/sdk/src/actions/multivault.ts), [FeeProxy execution](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/sdk/src/actions/fee-proxy.ts).

# Representation profiles

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/representation-profiles

Applies to V2 · `@0xintuition/iid` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/primitives` 0.1.0

A representation profile describes the atom data that carries an IID. P0 stores the bare canonical identifier, P1 adds the evidence needed to interpret or re-derive it, and P2 adds descriptive fields. The IID names the entity; the atom ID identifies the exact stored bytes, so different representations of one IID can have different atom IDs.

**Builds on:** IIDs and atoms.

**Implemented by:** [iid](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/iid), [primitives](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/primitives).

## How it works

The canonical rules are [IID spec §7.2](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-identifier/blob/3e593247c0e7cb168b37368937167ed146d3868a/spec/07-representation-profiles.md#72-the-profiles), [IID spec §7.3](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-identifier/blob/3e593247c0e7cb168b37368937167ed146d3868a/spec/07-representation-profiles.md#73-scheme-typing), and [IID spec §7.5](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-identifier/blob/3e593247c0e7cb168b37368937167ed146d3868a/spec/07-representation-profiles.md#75-requirements).

| Profile | Identity payload | When to use it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| P0 — anchor | Exact canonical IID text | Class A or B identifiers whose scheme is unambiguously typed |
| P1 — identity context | Type, IID, identity-recipe fields, and corroborating evidence | Required minimum for Class C or polymorphic identifiers |
| P2 — enriched | P1 plus descriptive data | Opt in when that description must be part of the atom |

Both P0 eligibility conditions must hold. A `gen1` identifier carries an entity type, but its Class C derivation still requires recipe evidence at P1. A plain name can be ambiguous; deterministic derivation cannot establish that two people with the same name are one person.

The pinned builder selects P0 when eligible and otherwise P1. An explicit ineligible P0 request returns errors. On its derived-IID path, explicit P1 and P2 currently serialize the same identified envelope: requesting P2 alone does not add a full descriptive payload. Its `candidateIid` path selects by eligibility and ignores the profile option. See the [builder source](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/primitives/src/anchor.ts) before relying on those options.

These rules follow `intuition-identifier` at the linked immutable revision. The pinned `@0xintuition/iid-spec` copy differs: it lacks §7.8, adds typed `wd` and weak `acct` forms, and includes additional schemes. The canonical specification governs this explanation; package behavior is documented separately in [iid-spec](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/iid-spec).

### Keep companion metadata outside identity

[IID spec §7.8](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-identifier/blob/3e593247c0e7cb168b37368937167ed146d3868a/spec/07-representation-profiles.md#78-the-atom-creation-model-data-and-companion-metadata) separates the identity payload from companion URI entries: leads for resolution, provenance, or richer descriptions. Identity validation and comparison must work without those entries.

For `buildIidAnchor`, changing only `contextUris` preserves `data`, `dataHex`, and `id`. A JSON-LD `@context` field **inside** the atom is different: changing it changes serialized bytes and can change the atom ID. The builder normalizes companion entries, but registering them still requires a URI-aware write; it does not fetch or upload them.

The specification's identity-canonical and display-canonical roles describe an equivalence architecture. They do not establish a cluster or election API in Core. Choosing a richer display source must not rewrite original atom IDs or move existing claims and positions.

## Representation profiles - Example

A name-derived person needs P1 evidence. This offline check confirms the default and the rejected bare-anchor request:

```ts
import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
import { buildIidAnchor } from '@0xintuition/primitives/anchor';

const fields = { givenName: 'Ada', familyName: 'Lovelace' };
const contextual = buildIidAnchor('person', fields);
if (!contextual.success) throw new Error(contextual.errors.join('; '));
assert.equal(contextual.value.profile, 'p1');
assert.equal(contextual.value.class, 'C');

const forcedAnchor = buildIidAnchor('person', fields, { profile: 'p0' });
assert.equal(forcedAnchor.success, false);
```

This uses the package's fixture fields to demonstrate representation selection, not to verify a real person's identity. The [quickstart](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/get-started/quickstart) separately proves that equivalent ISRC spellings and changed companion URIs preserve P0 bytes and IDs.

## Common mistakes

- Passing an IID where a protocol call expects a bytes32 term ID.
- Rebuilding an existing atom with a different profile and expecting its ID to stay unchanged.
- Treating companion `contextUris` as the JSON-LD `@context` inside atom data.
- Treating P2 selection as a provider fetch, or a valid IID as proof of a description.
- Requiring companion metadata to validate identity; missing context means unknown, not invalid.

## Next

[Protocol writes](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/protocol-writes) uses the selected bytes in a transaction plan. Keep them unchanged through review and submission.

# Write a classification plugin

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/core/classification-plugin

Applies to V2 · `@0xintuition/atom-classification` 0.1.0

Recognize a deliberate input pattern and emit a canonical classification through an explicitly registered plugin.

## Before you start

Use Node 22.18 or newer and install the public package:

```sh
npm install --save-exact @0xintuition/atom-classification@0.1.0 viem@2.31.4
```

A classifier decides whether it recognizes input; a resolver produces canonical candidates. This example recognizes an explicit `idea:` prefix offline. It does not infer that arbitrary prose names a unique entity, mint an IID, derive an atom ID, or persist a graph record.

## Steps

### 1. Declare the plugin and register its dependencies

A manifest declares identity, version, compatible engine range, runtime, capabilities, permissions, dependencies, provided features, and priority. Lower priorities run earlier. `type-profiles` supplies the type registry used by this resolver; the emitted `DefinedTerm` type must be registered.

```ts
import {
  createClientEngine,
  createTypeProfilesPlugin,
  validatePluginManifest,
  type AtomClassificationPlugin,
} from '@0xintuition/atom-classification';

export const ideaPlugin: AtomClassificationPlugin = {
  manifest: {
    id: 'example-idea',
    version: '1.0.0',
    engineRange: '^0.1.0',
    runtime: 'universal',
    priority: 30,
    capabilities: ['classifier:text:idea', 'resolver:lexical:defined-term'],
    permissions: [],
    dependsOn: ['type-profiles'],
    provides: ['example:idea'],
  },
  classifiers: [
    {
      id: 'idea-classifier',
      classify(input) {
        const name = input.startsWith('idea:') ? input.slice(5).trim() : '';
        return name
          ? {
              type: 'text',
              domain: 'lexical',
              subtype: 'idea',
              confidence: 1,
              meta: { name },
            }
          : null;
      },
    },
  ],
  resolvers: [
    {
      id: 'idea-resolver',
      executionMode: 'deterministic',
      canResolve: (classification) =>
        classification.domain === 'lexical' &&
        classification.subtype === 'idea',
      resolve: ({ request }) => ({
        classifications: [
          {
            type: 'DefinedTerm',
            data: {
              '@context': 'https://schema.org/',
              '@type': 'DefinedTerm',
              name: request.input.slice(5).trim(),
            },
          },
        ],
      }),
    },
  ],
};
validatePluginManifest(ideaPlugin.manifest);
const engine = createClientEngine({
  plugins: [createTypeProfilesPlugin(), ideaPlugin],
});
const input = 'idea: semantic grounding';
if (Buffer.byteLength(input, 'utf8') > 4_096)
  throw new Error('Input too large');
export const result = await engine.classify({
  input,
  mode: 'client-only',
  classificationSessionId: 'docs-plugin',
});
console.log(result.resolved?.publishable);
```

### 2. Keep matching deterministic and output canonical

Return `null` for unrelated input. Set the resolver's `executionMode: 'deterministic'` for this offline client flow: an omitted mode defaults to server enrichment and the client-only policy would skip that resolver. Prefer resolver `classifications` containing `type`, `data`, and optional metadata; the engine supplies missing plugin, provider, timestamp, and confidence metadata. `resolved.publishable` is the identity-oriented projection, while `resolved.classifications` may contain richer detail. Neither is proof of external truth.

The compatibility `atoms` projection still exists in the pinned implementation. If a resolver supplies both forms, the engine checks parity. Avoid introducing new dependencies on legacy-only fields. Declare permissions for capabilities you use; client runtimes cannot execute AI-capable plugins. Keep input byte and collection limits at the host boundary before parsing.

### 3. Test with fixed inputs

Run the complete [plugin helper](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-docs/blob/d137b0adacbfb9fda3b0d07d94e695ca4e7abc03/examples/v2/music-catalog/src/classification-plugin.ts) with `node`. Verify that the recognized input produces a `DefinedTerm` with name `semantic grounding`, unrelated input makes the classifier return `null`, and empty `idea:` input is rejected by the classifier. Compare semantic output across repeated runs; default timestamp metadata is time-dependent, so it is not part of a deterministic equality assertion.

Validate the manifest, test missing dependencies, and verify runtime restrictions before registering in a service. Test canonical/legacy parity only if you intentionally emit both forms.

### 4. Register at the host's composition boundary

The snippet passes an explicit plugin set to `createClientEngine`; registration is complete for that engine only. Adding a file to a repository does not install it into other engines.

In a fork of Core, inspect [the service runtime wrapper](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-core/blob/a402f880600f92969dc8fb013ca0f69fc9a02420/services/atom-services/src/service/runtime.ts). It calls the public package's `createAtomServicesProcessingRuntime`. That package accepts `pluginOverrides.classification`; the pinned Core wrapper's local option type does not expose that override. A fork owner must explicitly wire the chosen plugin set into the wrapper's runtime construction, preserve required built-ins, and rebuild the affected services.

The classification worker also reaches that runtime wrapper through [its engine setup](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-core/blob/a402f880600f92969dc8fb013ca0f69fc9a02420/services/workers/src/kg/atom-classification/index.ts). Review both call paths and deploy the rebuilt service and worker processes that should use the plugin. There is no documented directory loader, environment-variable plugin installer, or automatic registration across all running processes. The source setup workflow is [Query a Core node](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/query-core).

## Check the result

The offline helper validates the manifest and prints a publishable `DefinedTerm` envelope. This proves the local engine contract; Core registration and service execution require the fork's explicit source change and tests.

## Related

[Classify and enrich atoms](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/classify-enrich) and [atom classification](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/atom-classification).

Sources: [plugin authoring contract](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/atom-classification/docs/plugin-authoring.md), [external plugin example](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/examples/atom-classification-plugin/src/index.ts), [runtime override contract](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/atom-runtime/src/consumers.ts), and [Core classification guide](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-core/blob/a402f880600f92969dc8fb013ca0f69fc9a02420/docs/writing-a-classification-plugin.md).

# What you can build

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/examples

The packages supply shared identities and graph modeling tools. Core supplies storage, processing workers, and queries. Protocol contracts add registration and economic positions. Your application combines these with its own rules for evidence, permissions, and ranking.

## Build a music catalog

[Build a music catalog](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/examples/music-catalog) connects recording, artist, and album atoms with explicit triples. It uses clearly labeled synthetic identities, keeps display metadata separate, and shows where persistence and protocol planning fit.

Use the catalog to answer three questions: which entity is this, which bytes represent it, and which directed relationship am I asserting? Those answers transfer to other domains.

## Apply the pattern

| Application | Shared building blocks | Decisions your application owns |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Media discovery and curation | Identity ladders, Creation Profiles, explicit triples | Duplicate review, ranking, moderation |
| Research and evidence | Stable anchors, shared predicates, provenance | Evidence quality, citations, access control |
| Portable collections | Item IDs and containment relationships | Membership order, permissions, deletion semantics |
| Contextual reputation | Attributed claims and vault positions | Context, scoring, resistance to manipulation |
| Agent-assisted graph building | Offline builders and reviewed action plans | Scope, budget, provenance, authorization |
| Enrichment services | Parser, classifier, provider runtime | Provider terms, credentials, retries, cache policy |

These are application patterns; each still needs product-specific policy and implementation. A valid identifier does not prove a claim, and a position alone does not establish reputation.

For a smaller starting point, run the [offline quickstart](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/get-started/quickstart). For operational boundaries, read [How the pieces fit](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/get-started/how-it-fits).

Source: [What you can build with the packages](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/README.md#what-you-can-build).

# Build a music catalog

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/examples/music-catalog

Applies to V2 · `@0xintuition/primitives` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/classifications` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/iid` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/iid-registry` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/predicates` 0.1.0

**Time:** 15 minutes · **Steps:** 4

## What you'll build

Build three local entity anchors and two directed claims: a recording **byArtist** a performing identity, and a recording **inAlbum** an album release-group. Inspect their exact bytes, IIDs, profiles, and atom IDs before storing anything.

“One More Time”, “Daft Punk”, “Discovery”, and the accompanying identifiers are **synthetic test fixtures** adapted from package tests, not verified real-world records. The separate golden ISRC quickstart does not identify this synthetic recording. A recording is not its composition or remix, a performing identity is not necessarily a legal person, and a release-group is not one specific release edition.

## Before you start

Use Node 22.18 or newer. No wallet, RPC, API key, or running Core node is needed for the offline catalog. See [installation](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/install) for ESM and peer setup.

## Steps

### 1. Set up the project

```sh
mkdir music-catalog
cd music-catalog
npm init -y
npm pkg set type=module
npm install --save-exact @0xintuition/primitives@0.1.0 @0xintuition/ids@0.1.0 @0xintuition/iid@0.1.0 @0xintuition/iid-registry@0.1.0 viem@2.31.4
```

### 2. Choose representations and construct explicit edges

Save the complete example as `catalog.ts`:

```ts
import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
import { calculateAtomId } from '@0xintuition/ids';
import { inspectIntuitionId } from '@0xintuition/iid';
import { classificationForIid } from '@0xintuition/iid-registry';
import { buildIidAnchor } from '@0xintuition/primitives/anchor';
import { getPredicateInfo } from '@0xintuition/primitives/predicate';
import { buildTriple } from '@0xintuition/primitives/triple';
import type { BuildResult } from '@0xintuition/primitives';

function unwrap<T>(result: BuildResult<T>): T {
  if (!result.success) throw new Error(result.errors.join('; '));
  return result.value;
}

// Synthetic test identifiers, not verified MusicBrainz records.
const recordingValues = {
  name: 'One More Time',
  sameAs: [
    'https://musicbrainz.org/recording/b1a9c0e9-d987-4042-ae91-78d6a3267d69',
  ],
};
const recording = unwrap(buildIidAnchor('music-recording', recordingValues));
const artist = unwrap(buildIidAnchor('music-group', { name: 'Daft Punk' }));
const album = unwrap(
  buildIidAnchor('music-album', {
    name: 'Discovery',
    sameAs: [
      'https://musicbrainz.org/release-group/41b3f6ea-f7b6-3a6c-9a0a-3f8d6e2a1b55',
    ],
  }),
);
const byArtist = getPredicateInfo('byArtist');
const inAlbum = getPredicateInfo('inAlbum');
assert.ok(byArtist && inAlbum);

const claims = [
  unwrap(buildTriple(recording.id, byArtist.key, artist.id)),
  unwrap(buildTriple(recording.id, inAlbum.key, album.id)),
];
assert.equal(claims[0].predicateId, byArtist.id);
assert.equal(calculateAtomId(byArtist.atomData), byArtist.id);
assert.notEqual(
  unwrap(buildTriple(artist.id, byArtist.key, recording.id)).id,
  claims[0].id,
);

// Companion context travels alongside the atom; it is not atom data.
const withContext = unwrap(
  buildIidAnchor('music-recording', recordingValues, {
    contextUris: ['https://example.org/catalog/recording.json'],
  }),
);
assert.equal(withContext.id, recording.id);
assert.equal(withContext.data, recording.data);
const changedJson = artist.data.replace(
  'https://schema.org/',
  'https://schema.org',
);
assert.notEqual(calculateAtomId(changedJson), artist.id);

const repeated = unwrap(buildIidAnchor('music-recording', recordingValues));
assert.equal(repeated.id, recording.id);
const nameOnly = unwrap(
  buildIidAnchor('music-recording', { name: 'One More Time' }),
);
assert.notEqual(nameOnly.id, recording.id);
assert.equal(nameOnly.profile, 'p1');
assert.equal(inspectIntuitionId(recording.iid!).valid, true);
assert.equal(classificationForIid(recording.iid!)?.slug, 'music-recording');
assert.equal(classificationForIid('int:wd:Q42'), undefined);

const catalog = {
  synthetic: true,
  entities: [recording, artist, album].map(({ data, iid, profile, id }) => ({
    data,
    iid,
    profile,
    id,
  })),
  predicates: [byArtist, inAlbum].map(({ key, atomData, id }) => ({
    key,
    atomData,
    id,
  })),
  claims: claims.map((triple) => ({
    triple,
    source: 'local synthetic fixture',
  })),
};
console.log(JSON.stringify(catalog, null, 2));
console.log('3 entities, 2 predicate atoms, 2 directed claims');
console.log(
  `Profiles: ${catalog.entities.map((entity) => entity.profile).join(', ')}`,
);
console.log(
  'Context unchanged; reversed edge differs; bare Wikidata type unknown',
);
```

The recording and release-group use typed MusicBrainz fixtures and select `p0`, whose data is the bare IID. The artist uses a name-derived `p1` envelope. Its name is ambiguous; deterministic serialization does not establish unique real-world identity. The script's repeated recording import has the same bytes and ID, while the name-only recording uses a different representation and ID.

A predicate key such as `byArtist` selects a registry entry. That entry supplies canonical serialized atom data and its deterministic ID; it is not merely a label to hash. Both predicate atoms belong in the graph. `buildTriple` uses subject, predicate, and object in order. Reversing those roles produces a different claim, as the assertion demonstrates.

### 3. Inspect identity and context boundaries

The printed `entities` array contains exact `data`, `iid`, `profile`, and atom `id` values. The IID describes the selected identifier; the atom ID is derived from the serialized representation's bytes. `predicates` exposes each key, serialized data, and ID. `claims` retains the local fixture attribution.

The code proves that companion `contextUris` leave the data and atom ID unchanged. In contrast, changing JSON-LD `@context` inside the artist's serialized atom changes its bytes and ID. Do not confuse those two kinds of context. Name or label edits in a separate application presentation record need not rewrite existing atom data.

### 4. Plan the next boundary explicitly

Use [creation profiles](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/creation-profiles) to inspect fields and allowed relationship targets. A collected `byArtist` string is not the edge; this example creates the edge explicitly.

Follow [classify and enrich](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/classify-enrich) for separate parse, classify, provider-plan, fixture-execution, and provenance steps. A name-only input can remain a generic `Thing`; a valid IID can have no mapped type or available provider. Neither classification nor an enrichment artifact proves a real-world match.

To read shared records, [query your Core node](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/query-core). Choose whether to insert these exact records off-chain or create missing terms on-chain and wait for indexing. Local construction does not persist atoms. Preserve subject, predicate, and object data and verify that the required terms exist before writing triples.

## Run it

```sh
node catalog.ts
```

The script prints the complete catalog JSON and then these measured summary lines:

```text
3 entities, 2 predicate atoms, 2 directed claims
Profiles: p0, p1, p0
Context unchanged; reversed edge differs; bare Wikidata type unknown
```

Assertions check deduplication, profile selection, predicate identity, triple direction, context invariance, and an unmapped classification. These are local checks, not provider or chain verification.

## Full source

[Music catalog source project](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-docs/tree/d137b0adacbfb9fda3b0d07d94e695ca4e7abc03/examples/v2/music-catalog), including processing and plugin helpers. The catalog fixture is grounded in [pinned anchor tests](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/primitives/src/__tests__/anchor-parity.test.ts) and the [package lifecycle example](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/examples/hackathon-quickstart/src/package-lifecycle.ts).

## Next steps

Explore [representation profiles](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/representation-profiles), [predicate helpers](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/predicates), [action envelopes](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/action-plans), and [Core reads](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/query-core).

# How the pieces fit

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/get-started/how-it-fits

An Intuition application starts with the entity it wants to represent and the relationships it wants to assert. Public packages construct and interpret data; your application chooses storage, provider policy, authorization, and presentation.

## How it works

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  primitives["Protocol primitives"] --> identity["Intuition Identifier"] --> processing["Classification and enrichment"] --> writes["Protocol writes"] --> querying["Indexing and querying"]
  semantic["Semantic / data modeling"] -.-> primitives
  builders["Builder helpers"] -.-> primitives
  ids["Identity packages"] -.-> identity
  runtime["Pipeline runtime"] -.-> processing
  atoms["Atom processing"] -.-> processing
  app["Application integration"] -.-> writes
  protocol["Protocol plumbing"] -.-> writes
  core["Intuition Core"] -.-> querying
  core -.-> processing
```

Protocol primitives is ladder Tier 1, Intuition Identifier is Tier 2 (Identity), Classification and enrichment spans Tiers 3 and 4 (Meaning, Processing), and Protocol writes and Indexing and querying are Tier 5 (Data flow).

### Start with exact data

A recording is an entity; its atom is a particular representation. A P0 anchor stores canonical IID text, while a contextual representation stores a JSON object. Hashing the exact atom data produces its atom ID. Persist the bytes and ID together so later metadata updates do not silently create a different term.

A relationship is explicit: recording → **by artist** → artist. The predicate is itself an atom. Its registry key selects a definition; its serialized data determines its ID. A field named `artist` in a recording object does not create a triple, and reversing subject and object changes the statement.

### Choose packages by responsibility

| Layer | Packages | Responsibility |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Semantic / data modeling | `schema-org`, `classifications`, `predicates` | Shared vocabulary, input fields, and relationship suggestions |
| Identity | `iid-spec`, `iid`, `iid-registry`, `iid-ladder`, `ids` | Identifier rules, candidate selection, provider plans, and deterministic IDs |
| Builder helpers | `primitives` | Build atom data and explicit triples |
| Pipeline runtime | `pipeline-runtime` | Concurrency, cancellation, and circuit breaking |
| Atom processing | `atom-parser`, `atom-classification`, `atom-enrichment`, `atom-runtime` | Parse inputs, run plugins, and execute configured providers |
| Application integration | `sdk`, `cli` | Prepare actions, serializable envelopes, and calldata |
| Protocol plumbing | `protocol`, `deployments`, `periphery`, `curves`, `react` | Contract calls, deployment metadata, curve math, and hooks |

These are responsibility groups. The [runtime dependency graph](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/docs/architecture/dependency-graph.md) shows actual package dependencies. Importing a package does not start a worker or fetch provider data.

### Add persistence and transactions deliberately

Local modeling needs no chain or Core node. RPC reads inspect a selected contract's current state. Preparing an action may use those reads; submitting it requires an authorized signer. A transaction hash, a successful receipt, and visibility in an index are three different results.

[Core's architecture](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-core/blob/a402f880600f92969dc8fb013ca0f69fc9a02420/docs/architecture.md) adds durable storage, event ingestion, projections, processing workers, and the Query API. Its source Compose workflow starts the API and processing services; chain ingestion requires the indexing profile and explicit chain configuration. Read the indexed graph through [a Core node you run](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/query-core). An authenticated off-chain API insert is separate from a chain transaction.

Keep provider secrets on your server. Your application owns access control, evidence acceptance, ranking, and the meaning it assigns to vault positions. A shared ID or a large position does not establish that a claim is true.

## Related

- [Building blocks](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts) explains atoms, triples, and signals.
- [Offline quickstart](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/get-started/quickstart) proves identity and companion-context invariance.
- [Package reference](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages) gives public imports and runtime requirements.
- [Protocol writes](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/protocol-writes) separates planning, signing, and observation.
- [Compatibility](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/compatibility) covers peers, contract artifacts, and the pinned Core source.

Source: [Package layers](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/README.md#package-layers).

# Migrate from V1

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/get-started/migrate-from-v1

Applies to V2 · `@0xintuition/sdk` 4.0.0 · `@0xintuition/protocol` 4.0.0 · `@0xintuition/ids` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/predicates` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/primitives` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/cli` 0.1.0

Move an existing integration to the V2 package boundaries without silently changing historical atom bytes, IDs, claims, or positions.

## Before you start

Keep your existing lockfile and a fixture set of stored atom data, atom IDs, and ordered triples. Read [representation profiles](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/representation-profiles), [compatibility](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/compatibility), and [installation](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/install). Add readers for new representations before enabling new writers.

### What changed

V1 covers the `intuition-ts` packages and `intuition-rs` services. V2 covers the packages in the [release manifest](https://docs.intuition.systems/intuition-release.json) and Intuition Core. The generation label is independent of package semver.

Since the stable release on November 12, 2026, an untagged or `latest` install of the SDK or protocol selects the V2 package. To maintain V1, preserve `@0xintuition/sdk` 3.0.1, `@0xintuition/protocol` 2.0.3, and `@0xintuition/graphql` 3.0.1 in your lockfile. Frozen V1 pages still contain some untagged installs; do not assume every historical install command preserves those versions.

The V2 SDK root no longer exports the entire protocol or ID surface. Atom builders, shared predicates, identity selection, and transaction planning now have focused public packages. Core is a source application you fork and run; it is separate from installing the libraries.

## Steps

### 1. Map your packages

| V1 responsibility | V2 replacement | Migration check |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `@0xintuition/sdk` | `sdk` plus `ids`, `predicates`, and `primitives` | Replace removed root exports and separate local building from writes |
| `@0xintuition/protocol` | `protocol` plus `deployments`, `periphery`, and `curves` | Select the deployed implementation and its public artifacts |
| `@0xintuition/graphql` | No V2 package counterpart | Read the Query API of [a Core node you run](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/query-core) |
| `intuition-cli` | `@0xintuition/cli` | Use encoders; move client-free plans to SDK envelopes |
| Application-local type and predicate maps | `classifications` and `predicates` | Preserve canonical slugs, serialized predicate data, and IDs |
| Upload helper | Application-owned storage provider | Preserve existing content URIs; upload and protocol registration are separate operations |

Install exact versions for the packages you import directly and commit your lockfile. The [package catalog](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages) lists public entry points and peers.

### 2. Update imports

A V1 import can combine broad helpers at the SDK root:

```ts
import { calculateAtomId, createAtomFromString } from '@0xintuition/sdk';

export const legacyHelpers = { calculateAtomId, createAtomFromString };
```

For V2, choose each package's public entry point:

```ts
import { calculateAtomId } from '@0xintuition/ids';
import { PREDICATE_IDS } from '@0xintuition/predicates';
import { multivaultPrepareDepositTx } from '@0xintuition/sdk/actions';
import { getMultiVaultAddressFromChainId } from '@0xintuition/protocol';

export const migrationImports = {
  calculateAtomId,
  PREDICATE_IDS,
  multivaultPrepareDepositTx,
  getMultiVaultAddressFromChainId,
};
```

The SDK root retains selected ID helpers, but `ids` is the full deterministic-ID package. `sdk/utils` contains formatting utilities. Import low-level protocol APIs from `@0xintuition/protocol`, or use the explicit `@0xintuition/sdk/protocol` escape hatch. Bytecode belongs to `deployments/bytecode` or `protocol/contracts`; curve math belongs to `curves`.

### 3. Replace atom creation

V1 combines creation with a string or uploaded Thing workflow. These functions submit when called:

```ts
import { createAtomFromString, createAtomFromThing } from '@0xintuition/sdk';

type LegacyWriteConfig = Parameters<typeof createAtomFromString>[0];

export function createLegacyText(config: LegacyWriteConfig, text: string) {
  return createAtomFromString(config, text);
}

export function createLegacyThing(
  config: LegacyWriteConfig,
  thing: Parameters<typeof createAtomFromThing>[1],
) {
  return createAtomFromThing(config, thing);
}
```

For new V2 entities, build data first. `buildThing` preserves the descriptive JSON-LD builder pattern; `buildIidAnchor` selects an identity representation. They return a checked `BuildResult`, not a transaction receipt. Neither performs an upload.

The following helper demonstrates the separate write boundary. **Calling it simulates and submits a wallet transaction.** It is a migration reference, not part of the offline quickstart. The caller must choose a compatible deployment and creator, read current creation cost and URI limits, check existence, and supply assets in base units before invocation.

```ts
import { buildIidAnchor } from '@0xintuition/primitives/anchor';
import { multiVaultCreateAtomsWithUris } from '@0xintuition/protocol';
import type { AtomUriLimits, WriteConfig } from '@0xintuition/protocol';
import { stringToHex, type Address } from 'viem';

// Calling this function simulates and submits a wallet transaction.
export async function createRecording(
  config: WriteConfig,
  creator: Address,
  isrc: string,
  assets: bigint,
  uriLimits: AtomUriLimits,
) {
  const result = buildIidAnchor('music-recording', { isrc });
  if (!result.success) throw new Error(result.errors.join('; '));
  const atom = result.value;
  const transactionHash = await multiVaultCreateAtomsWithUris(config, {
    args: [
      creator,
      [atom.dataHex],
      [assets],
      [atom.contextUris.map((uri) => stringToHex(uri))],
    ],
    value: assets,
    uriLimits,
  });
  return { atom, transactionHash };
}
```

This helper uses no companion URIs, so its URI list is empty. If your application adds them, pass the builder's normalized `contextUris` through the URI-aware operation. Its `value` must equal the assets sum. A submitted hash still needs a successful receipt and event parsing scoped to the expected emitting contract.

An existing V1 string or IPFS URI is not automatically equivalent to a new IID anchor. Preserve the original bytes and ID; creating an anchor is a separate graph decision.

### 4. Replace triple creation

V1 wraps the contract operation and returns its event state:

```ts
import { createTripleStatement } from '@0xintuition/sdk';

export function createLegacyTriple(
  config: Parameters<typeof createTripleStatement>[0],
  input: Parameters<typeof createTripleStatement>[1],
) {
  return createTripleStatement(config, input);
}
```

V2 can calculate the ID locally and submit through the explicit protocol wrapper. The function below submits when invoked; its subject, predicate, and object atoms must already exist on the selected deployment.

```ts
import { calculateTripleId } from '@0xintuition/ids';
import {
  multiVaultCreateTriples,
  type WriteConfig as TripleWriteConfig,
} from '@0xintuition/protocol';
import type { Hex } from 'viem';

// The three atoms must already exist on the selected deployment.
export async function createRelationship(
  config: TripleWriteConfig,
  subject: Hex,
  predicate: Hex,
  object: Hex,
  assets: bigint,
) {
  const id = calculateTripleId(subject, predicate, object);
  const transactionHash = await multiVaultCreateTriples(config, {
    args: [[subject], [predicate], [object], [assets]],
    value: assets,
  });
  return { id, transactionHash };
}
```

Preserve subject–predicate–object order. Use the predicate registry's serialized data and ID; a registry key or display label alone is not the predicate atom. Reversing a triple changes its meaning and ID. Handle a reverted receipt or no matching creation event explicitly.

### 5. Move reads

A V1 read uses `getAtomDetails`:

```ts
import { getAtomDetails } from '@0xintuition/sdk';

export function readLegacyAtom(atomId: string) {
  return getAtomDetails(atomId);
}
```

For V2 indexed graph data, [query a Core node you run](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/query-core). Keep missing records and indexing delay visible to callers. Contract reads through protocol helpers read chain state, which is a separate data source.

The V2 SDK's `@0xintuition/sdk/api` client and its `atoms.getById` still call the hosted V1 GraphQL API. They are not a V2 read path; [The SDK read client](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/read-with-sdk) documents that boundary. Existing GraphQL queries stay with the supported [V1 API documentation](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/v1/graphql-api/overview).

### 6. Preserve identity

Keep the exact stored string when re-deriving a historical atom ID:

```ts
import { calculateAtomId as atomIdFromData } from '@0xintuition/ids';
import { stringToHex as encodeData } from 'viem';

export function preserveAtom(data: string) {
  return { data, dataHex: encodeData(data), id: atomIdFromData(data) };
}
```

Compare the result against your stored ID before switching. Do not parse and serialize JSON again just to normalize it: field order, whitespace, schema context strings, and payload changes can alter bytes and IDs. Do not rebuild an existing atom under another profile.

Companion `contextUris` are distinct from JSON-LD `@context` inside atom data. Metadata can be refreshed separately; changing identity-bearing fields creates another representation. Preserve historical claims and positions on their original terms, and model reviewed equivalence with explicit attributed relationships.

### 7. Move agent and CLI plans

Client-free, JSON-serializable envelope builders now live in `@0xintuition/sdk/actions`. For example, the deprecated CLI library name `buildMultiVaultDepositPlan` maps to `multiVaultDepositEnvelope`; `buildFeeProxyCreateAtomsWithUrisPlan` maps to `feeProxyCreateAtomsWithUrisEnvelope`.

The `intuition` executable exposes encoder commands, not a plan command. Envelope builders consume caller-supplied read context; quote and preparation helpers may perform RPC reads, while execution helpers can submit. See [action plans](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/action-plans) for the reviewed-plan workflow and the [source alias table](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/sdk/docs/action-plans.md) for all mappings.

Require human review of signer, chain, destination, receiver, value, and limits before signing or submission. Keep already mined steps recorded if a multi-step execution later fails.

## Check the result

Your integration should compile against the exact V2 packages, preserve every historical fixture's bytes and ID, and explicitly handle `BuildResult` errors, absent records, reverted receipts, and partial enrichment. Check that indexed reads use your Core adapter and that offline previews cannot invoke write helpers.

Treat compilation and fixture checks as their own evidence. They do not prove a deployment supports every ABI operation or that a transaction was submitted successfully.

# Quickstart: an atom ID and IID offline

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/get-started/quickstart

Applies to V2 · `@0xintuition/primitives` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/iid` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/iid-registry` 0.1.0

**Time:** 10 minutes · **Steps:** 6

## What you'll build

Turn the ISRC spelling `US-RC1-76-07839` into the canonical IID `int:isrc:USRC17607839`, a P0 representation, and a deterministic atom ID. The code also proves that equivalent ISRC spellings and different companion context URIs produce the same atom bytes and ID.

This is the packages' golden canonicalization fixture. It is separate from the synthetic recording identities in the music catalog; no recording title or artist is inferred from it.

## Before you start

Use **Node 22.18 or newer** to run TypeScript directly. Installation needs npm registry access. After installation, the example runs offline with no wallet, RPC, API key, or account. It creates no remote or on-chain record.

## Steps

### 1. Check Node

```sh
node --version
```

Confirm the version is at least `v22.18.0`.

### 2. Create an ESM project

```sh
mkdir intuition-quickstart
cd intuition-quickstart
npm init -y
npm pkg set type=module
```

### 3. Install the pinned builder

```sh
npm install @0xintuition/primitives@0.1.0
```

Keep the generated lockfile. See [installation](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/install) for other package combinations and declared peers.

### 4. Save the offline example

Create `quickstart.ts`:

```ts
import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
import { buildIidAnchor } from '@0xintuition/primitives/anchor';

const result = buildIidAnchor(
  'music-recording',
  { isrc: 'US-RC1-76-07839' },
  { contextUris: ['https://example.com/recordings/1'] },
);
if (!result.success) throw new Error(result.errors.join('; '));
const atom = result.value;
assert.equal(atom.iid, 'int:isrc:USRC17607839');
assert.equal(atom.profile, 'p0');
assert.equal(atom.data, atom.iid);

const otherContext = buildIidAnchor(
  'music-recording',
  { isrc: 'USRC17607839' },
  { contextUris: ['https://example.org/alternate-evidence'] },
);
if (!otherContext.success) throw new Error(otherContext.errors.join('; '));
assert.equal(otherContext.value.data, atom.data);
assert.equal(otherContext.value.dataHex, atom.dataHex);
assert.equal(otherContext.value.id, atom.id);

console.log(atom.iid);
console.log(atom.profile);
console.log(atom.dataHex);
console.log(atom.id);
```

`success` distinguishes a valid result from structured errors. `data` is the exact canonical IID text for this P0 atom, `dataHex` encodes those bytes, and `id` is the bytes32 protocol atom ID. Companion `contextUris` are discovery information; this code neither fetches nor uploads them.

### 5. Run the example

```sh
node quickstart.ts
```

Compare the four lines with **Run it** below. Keep the IID, profile, exact data, hex bytes, atom ID, and original identity evidence together. Deriving an ID does not prove that an atom exists on a chain or in a Core node.

### 6. Optionally inspect the IID

```sh
npm install @0xintuition/iid@0.1.0 @0xintuition/iid-registry@0.1.0
```

Save as `inspect.ts`, then run `node inspect.ts`:

```ts
import { inspectIntuitionId } from '@0xintuition/iid';
import { classificationForIid } from '@0xintuition/iid-registry';

const iid = 'int:isrc:USRC17607839';
const inspection = inspectIntuitionId(iid);
if (!inspection.valid) throw new Error(inspection.reason);
const classification = classificationForIid(iid);
console.log(inspection.valid);
console.log(classification?.slug ?? 'No classification match');
```

This fixture prints `true` and `music-recording`. Other inputs can be invalid or have no unambiguous classification. Inspection and classification lookup do not execute provider requests.

## Run it

```sh
node quickstart.ts
```

Expected output from the pinned packages:

```text
int:isrc:USRC17607839
p0
0x696e743a697372633a555352433137363037383339
0xd3368a8190d3afd5fb05abd01db8141c09a77c3f290bb7a0ef2ffb2b5acab8d8
```

The last line is an atom ID, not an IID string. The assertions run before any output; an assertion failure or builder error stops execution.

## Next steps

- [Representation profiles](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/representation-profiles) explains when an IID needs contextual atom data.
- [Build a music catalog](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/examples/music-catalog) adds explicit artist and album triples using synthetic fixtures.
- [Protocol writes](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/protocol-writes) explains the separate transaction lifecycle.

Sources: [Getting started](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/docs/getting-started.md), [golden anchor tests](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/primitives/src/__tests__/anchor.test.ts).

# Versions and release status

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/get-started/versions

Applies to V2 · `@0xintuition/atom-classification` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/atom-enrichment` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/atom-parser` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/atom-runtime` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/classifications` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/cli` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/curves` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/deployments` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/ids` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/iid` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/iid-ladder` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/iid-registry` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/iid-spec` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/periphery` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/pipeline-runtime` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/predicates` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/primitives` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/protocol` 4.0.0 · `@0xintuition/react` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/schema-org` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/sdk` 4.0.0

**V2 is a generation, not a package semver.** It covers the packages in the release manifest and Intuition Core. Each npm package has its own version. **V1** covers the `intuition-ts` packages and `intuition-rs` services; those docs remain available at [V1](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/v1).

The documented package release is published and stable. Install the exact versions below and retain your lockfile. The [release manifest](https://docs.intuition.systems/intuition-release.json) records package versions, entry points, peers, engines, registry integrity, and immutable source provenance.

## Core source

Core is a repository to fork, clone, build, and run. These docs pin [Core source revision `a402f880600f92969dc8fb013ca0f69fc9a02420`](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-core/blob/a402f880600f92969dc8fb013ca0f69fc9a02420/README.md). That identifies source code; it does not name an npm distribution or attest to a published container image.

[Query a Core node](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/query-core) contains the source setup path. Default startup does not ingest chain events; indexing is an explicitly configured profile. Package installation, Core startup, and chain indexing are separate steps.

## Verified install hazards

At the 2026-11-17 registry check, `@0xintuition/sdk@alpha` selected `4.0.0-alpha.0`, and `@0xintuition/protocol@alpha` selected `3.0.0-alpha.0`, both superseded by the documented pins. Also, `@0xintuition/protocol@3` and `^3.0.0-alpha.0` resolve to the older stable `3.0.0` release. Those selectors do not select the V2 protocol pin. Dist-tags move; prefer exact versions.

The checked `latest` tags match the documented pins. An untagged install still follows a moving tag, so it is unsuitable for preserving a V1 dependency set or reproducing this documentation later.

## Upgrading

Use [Migrate from V1](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/get-started/migrate-from-v1) for breaking changes and identity preservation. [Compatibility](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/compatibility) separates package peers, example runtime pins, contract artifacts, and Core requirements.

Source: [Package release policy](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/docs/release.md).

# Intuition developer docs

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs

Intuition is an identity and knowledge graph protocol. Its packages help applications identify entities consistently, connect them with explicit relationships, and prepare actions through which people signal what they trust.

An **atom** stores a chosen representation as bytes. Its **atom ID** identifies those exact bytes. An **Intuition Identifier (IID)** names the represented entity; the same IID can appear in different representations. A **triple** connects a subject, predicate, and object in that order.

## Choose your path

| I want to… | Start here | Then build |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Build an application | [Derive an atom ID offline](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/get-started/quickstart) | [A music catalog](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/examples/music-catalog) with explicit recording, artist, and album relationships |
| Build with agents | [Read the agent contract](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/agents) | [Review action plans](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/action-plans) before a human authorizes execution |
| Run Core | [Query a Core node](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/query-core) | Fork, pin, build, and run the source to own graph storage and reads |
| Extend processing | [Classify and enrich inputs](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/classify-enrich) | [Write a classification plugin](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/core/classification-plugin) for your domain |

You can build identities and triples offline before choosing a wallet or backend. Processing, persistence, protocol submission, and indexing each have their own lifecycle; [How the pieces fit](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/get-started/how-it-fits) explains the boundaries.

## Explore the documentation

- [Concepts](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts) introduces representations, directed relationships, and protocol writes.
- [Examples](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/examples) connects the building blocks in a worked catalog.
- [Packages](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages) covers every published library; the [SDK reference](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/sdk) lists action signatures.
- [Install agent skills](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/agents/skills) for contract-level guidance, or [get help](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/community).

## Versions and source

**V2 names a generation**, covering the packages in the [release manifest](https://docs.intuition.systems/intuition-release.json) and Intuition Core. The packages are published as stable npm releases; each example uses exact pins. See [versions and release status](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/get-started/versions).

Core is a source application you fork, build, and run. These docs describe [Core source at the pinned revision](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-core/blob/a402f880600f92969dc8fb013ca0f69fc9a02420/README.md). The source pin identifies code, rather than an npm distribution or a released container image. The default source stack requires its indexing profile and chain configuration to start chain ingestion.

The [V1 documentation](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/v1) covers the `intuition-ts` packages and `intuition-rs` services. For agents, use the [V1 documentation index](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/v1/llms.txt). Start with [Migrate from V1](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/get-started/migrate-from-v1) when moving an integration.

Source: [Package concepts and application patterns](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/README.md#core-concepts).

## Runtime requirements

Packages are ESM-only: use named imports and set `"type": "module"` for Node applications. The manifest lists the engines and peers declared by each published package. The documentation's checks use an isolated dependency tree under `examples/v2`; V1 examples use separate V1 dependencies.

| Surface | Requirements or exact documentation pins |
| --- | --- |
| Direct TypeScript quickstart | Node 22.18 or newer |
| Example compiler | TypeScript 5.9.3; strict application checking, library declaration checking skipped |
| Contract clients | viem 2.31.4 in the checked examples; satisfy each package's declared peers |
| React example environment | React and React DOM 19.1.0; wagmi 2.15.4; TanStack Query 5.90.2 |
| Example type packages | Node types 22.20.5; React types 19.1.10; React DOM types 19.1.11 |
| Parser remote inspection | Node-compatible DNS/HTTP transport, Fetch, and Web Streams; choose runtime-compatible entry points |
| Classification and enrichment | Explicit plugins, provider configuration, credentials where needed, and cache policy |
| Core source workflow | Git, Bun 1.3.11, Node 20 or newer, Docker Compose v2 with a running Docker daemon, and curl |

The React package declares React 18+, wagmi 2+, TanStack Query 5+, viem 2, and the manifest's protocol/deployments package lines as peers. Keep your application's React and renderer versions aligned. Provider secrets belong on a backend; local parsing does not imply that remote enrichment works without network access.

## Contract artifacts and deployments

The package artifacts come from `@0xintuition/contracts-v2@1.1.0-alpha.1` and `@0xintuition/contracts-v2-periphery@1.1.0-alpha.0`. Their versioning is separate from the stable library release. [Artifact provenance](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/docs/contract-artifacts.md) verifies bundled interfaces and bytecode; it does not deploy or upgrade a contract.

Select addresses and check the implementation on your target chain before enabling URI creation, payable multicall, dynamic-fee, or on-behalf-of operations. The published deployment catalog withholds a TrustSwapAndBridgeRouter address; its lookup throws. See [deployments](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/deployments) and [protocol](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/protocol).

Ordinary React atom-creation hooks use `createAtoms`. For companion URI registration, use the explicit URI-aware protocol operation and your own transaction flow.

## Core source and package parity

Core source: [a402f880600f92969dc8fb013ca0f69fc9a02420](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-core/blob/a402f880600f92969dc8fb013ca0f69fc9a02420/README.md). Fork and build that revision following [Query a Core node](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/query-core). The source revision does not imply an npm installation of Core or equivalence with a released image.

At this source revision, [Core's committed lockfile](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-core/blob/a402f880600f92969dc8fb013ca0f69fc9a02420/bun.lock) resolves 17 manifest packages, all at their documented versions. SDK, CLI, React, and periphery are absent from its resolved package graph; absence is not a version mismatch. Separately versioned contract artifacts and Core workspace packages are outside that comparison.

The default stack starts Query API and processing services; it does not start chain ingestion without the indexing profile and chain configuration. API liveness alone does not prove that events have been indexed or external providers have enriched a record.

# @0xintuition/atom-classification

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/atom-classification

Applies to V2 · `@0xintuition/atom-classification` 0.1.0

## What it's for

A plugin engine that classifies input and resolves canonical envelopes in client-only, progressive, or server-only modes. It executes classification logic; the classifications package owns the canonical entity specifications.

## When to use it

Use it to turn an input into typed identity data before enrichment or a creation decision. Select plugins explicitly: creating an engine neither installs every provider nor persists output. Use server-compatible plugins for credentialed providers; a provider factory's existence does not guarantee a network response.

## Install

```sh
npm install @0xintuition/atom-classification@0.1.0
```

Use ESM on Node 20+ or Bun for server execution. A client engine needs client-compatible plugins; provider requests require a suitable transport.

## Entry points

All public modules

| --- | --- |

| `./ai` | Optional server AI fallback adapter |
| `./cache` | Resolver cache contracts and adapters |
| `./client` | Client engine factory |
| `./engine` | Shared classification engine |
| `./plugin-factories` | Built-in plugin factories |
| `./plugins` | Plugin manifests, types, and validation |
| `./plugins/amazon` | Amazon plugin and adapters |
| `./plugins/default-url` | Generic URL fallback |
| `./plugins/etherscan` | Etherscan plugin |

| `./plugins/github` | GitHub plugin and adapters |
| `./plugins/imdb` | IMDb plugin and adapters |
| `./plugins/instagram` | Instagram plugin and adapters |
| `./plugins/isbn` | ISBN plugin |
| `./plugins/lexical` | Opt-in lexical classification |
| `./plugins/plain-text` | Generic Thing fallback for text |
| `./plugins/spotify` | Spotify plugin and adapters |
| `./plugins/tiktok` | TikTok plugin |
| `./plugins/tmdb` | TMDB plugin |

## Depends on and works with

Runtime package dependencies: [atom-enrichment](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/atom-enrichment), [atom-parser](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/atom-parser), [classifications](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/classifications), [iid](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/iid), [iid-ladder](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/iid-ladder), [iid-registry](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/iid-registry), [pipeline-runtime](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/pipeline-runtime), [predicates](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/predicates), [primitives](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/primitives), and [schema-org](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/schema-org). Peer dependencies: none. `zod` is an additional ordinary dependency in the package manifest.

Classification consumes enrichment helpers; enrichment does not depend on this engine. Your host owns credentials, persistent storage, cache selection, and request policy.

## @0xintuition/atom-classification - Example

An explicit pair of local plugins produces a generic Thing for fixed text. An empty plugin set demonstrates the unmatched-text fallback; the invalid request demonstrates boundary failure without a provider call.

```ts
import {
  classifyOutcome,
  createClientEngine,
  createPlainTextPlugin,
  createTypeProfilesPlugin,
} from '@0xintuition/atom-classification';

const engine = createClientEngine({
  plugins: [createTypeProfilesPlugin(), createPlainTextPlugin()],
  now: () => new Date('2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z'),
});
export const classified = await engine.classify({
  input: 'A synthetic catalog idea',
  mode: 'client-only',
  classificationSessionId: 'package-reference',
});
console.log(classified.resolved?.publishable[0]?.type);

// Unmatched text remains a candidate Thing, not a verified identity.
export const unmatched = await createClientEngine({ plugins: [] }).classify({
  input: 'Unmatched synthetic catalog label',
  mode: 'client-only',
  classificationSessionId: 'unmatched-fixture',
});
console.log(unmatched.resolved?.fallbackUsed);

export const invalidRequest = await classifyOutcome(engine, {
  input: '',
  mode: 'client-only',
  classificationSessionId: 'invalid-fixture',
});
console.log(invalidRequest.kind);
```

Read `resolved.classifications` for canonical envelopes and `resolved.publishable` for the identity-safe projection. Identity fields are eligible by default, approved rich fields depend on source policy, and volatile fields are excluded. `resolved.atoms` is a compatibility projection. These are candidate payloads, not proof of an on-chain atom.

A completed response's `ok: true` does not promise full resolution: inspect `status` (`placeholder`, `partial`, or `complete`), optional `resolved`, and `resolverErrors`. Unmatched text falls back to a generic Thing with `resolved.fallbackUsed: true`; that candidate is not a verified entity identity. Invalid requests reject `classify`; `classifyOutcome` captures that rejection as an outcome. Cancellation and resolver deadlines are separate from a successful partial result.

External plugins implement `AtomClassificationPlugin` with a validated manifest, classifiers, and resolvers. Register emitted types, satisfy `dependsOn`, and explicitly set a local resolver's `executionMode: 'deterministic'` when it should run under client-only policy. An omitted mode defaults to server enrichment. Follow [Write a classification plugin](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/core/classification-plugin) for the complete contract and Core composition boundary.

## Related concepts

[Representation profiles](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/representation-profiles) separates entity identity from its serialized payload. [Classify and enrich atoms](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/classify-enrich) explains the handoff to enrichment.

# @0xintuition/atom-enrichment

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/atom-enrichment

Applies to V2 · `@0xintuition/atom-enrichment` 0.1.0

## What it's for

Run provider plugins against classified input and collect typed artifacts with provenance. Extraction can turn those artifacts into classification fields; neither operation changes an existing atom's identity bytes.

## When to use it

Use it when you need provider metadata, a selected provider plan, or normalized fields with missing-field diagnostics. Use the IID registry to plan providers before execution. A plan is not a completed lookup, and an artifact is not evidence that every required classification field was extracted.

## Install

```sh
npm install @0xintuition/atom-enrichment@0.1.0
```

Use typed ESM on Node 20+ or Bun. Real providers may require HTTP access, credentials, and server-compatible execution; inject those deliberately.

## Entry points

All public modules

| Subpath | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `.` | Engine, providers, registries, presets, handoff, and public types |
| `./types` | Inputs, artifacts, results, and request schemas |
| `./handoff` | Adapt classification results into enrichment input |
| `./provider-data` | Normalized provider payload types |
| `./plugins` | Plugin manifests, contracts, and validation |
| `./providers` | Provider factories and request helpers |
| `./presets` | Provider bundles and explicit environment mapping |
| `./engine` | Enrichment execution engine |
| `./plugin-registry` | Register and resolve plugins |
| `./cache` | Cache contracts and memory or HTTP adapters |
| `./testing` | Deterministic fixtures and plugin conformance helpers |
| `./classifications` | Provider artifact classification registry |
| `./classifications/defaults` | Built-in artifact definitions |
| `./classifications/registry` | Artifact registration and validation |
| `./classifications/schemas` | Artifact payload schemas |
| `./provider-external-data` | External provider response schemas |
| `./provider-plan` | Match desired providers against installed capabilities |
| `./slug-aliases` | Canonicalize provider slug aliases |
| `./extraction` | Extract normalized classification fields and provenance |
| `./data-resolved-schema` | Normalized resolved-data boundary |
| `./spotify-client` | Shared Spotify client |
| `./tmdb-request-observer` | Observe TMDB requests |
| `./provider-fetch` | Provider transport helpers |
| `./plugin-api` | Public plugin authoring API |
| `./outcome` | Promise outcome wrapper for enrichment |
| `./adapters/upstash` | Explicit HTTP cache adapter |
| `./ssrf` | Pinned transport and destination policy helpers |
| `./identifier-rung-projection` | Project admissible identifier rungs |
| `./url-hygiene` | URL normalization policy |

## Depends on and works with

Runtime package dependencies: [classifications](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/classifications), [iid](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/iid), [iid-ladder](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/iid-ladder), [iid-registry](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/iid-registry), [pipeline-runtime](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/pipeline-runtime), [protocol](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/protocol), and [schema-org](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/schema-org). Peer dependencies: none. `zod` is an additional ordinary dependency in the package manifest.

Canonical entity requirements belong to classifications. This package's artifact registry validates provider payloads. `toClassifiedAtomInput` returns usable input or `null`; handle that boundary before calling `enrich`. `createIdentifierProviderPlan` records scheduled, unavailable, and unsupported providers instead of silently treating a missing plugin as completed work.

## @0xintuition/atom-enrichment - Example

These two synthetic plugins exercise the real engine without network access. One returns a valid Open Graph artifact; the other rejects. The example preserves the successful artifact alongside the failure.

```ts
import {
  createEnrichmentEngine,
  type EnrichmentPlugin,
} from '@0xintuition/atom-enrichment';

// Synthetic fixtures: no HTTP provider, credentials, or fetched page.
const fixture: EnrichmentPlugin = {
  id: 'catalog-fixture',
  version: '1.0.0',
  runtime: 'universal',
  artifactTypes: ['opengraph'],
  supports: (request) => request.input.atomType === 'thing',
  enrich: async (_request, { now }) => [
    {
      artifact_type: 'opengraph',
      data: { title: 'Synthetic catalog' },
      meta: {
        pluginId: 'catalog-fixture',
        provider: 'offline-fixture',
        fetchedAt: now(),
      },
    },
  ],
};
const unavailable: EnrichmentPlugin = {
  ...fixture,
  id: 'unavailable-fixture',
  enrich: async () => {
    throw new Error('Fixture provider unavailable');
  },
};

const engine = createEnrichmentEngine({
  plugins: [fixture, unavailable],
  now: () => '2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z',
});
export const enriched = await engine.enrich({
  runtime: 'server',
  input: {
    atomType: 'thing',
    jsonLd: { '@context': 'https://schema.org/', '@type': 'Thing' },
    source: {
      classificationEngine: 'offline-fixture',
      classifiedAt: '2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z',
    },
  },
});
console.log(enriched.status, enriched.artifacts.length, enriched.errors.length);
```

The result is `partial` with one artifact and one error. Inspect `status`, `artifacts`, `errors`, `skipped`, and `timings`; do not discard useful artifacts because a provider failed. Invalid request schemas can still reject before provider execution. Runtime mismatches and unsupported inputs can produce skipped providers.

Preserve each artifact's `meta.pluginId`, `provider`, `fetchedAt`, and optional `sourceUrl`. Here the provider is explicitly an offline fixture, not a scraped page. For real providers, select a small preset and supply approved transports, credentials, timeouts, and cache policy. A keyless service can still make network calls. Spotify's URL-derived fallback, for example, is distinct from a credentialed Web API artifact.

`extractClassificationFields` reports values, provenance, missing required fields, and dropped-field reasons; it may perform additional lookups. The pinned MusicBrainz artifact does not automatically supply extracted music-recording fields. The [processing guide](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/classify-enrich) demonstrates that partial boundary with a fixed fixture. Your application owns retries, queues, persistence, and access control.

## Related concepts

[Representation profiles](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/representation-profiles) distinguishes companion metadata from identity bytes. [Classify and enrich atoms](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/classify-enrich) shows provider planning, execution, and extraction together.
