[Package README](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/atom-enrichment/README.md), [provider payload documentation](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/atom-enrichment/docs/README.md), [plugin contract](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/atom-enrichment/src/plugins.ts), and [partial-result tests](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/atom-enrichment/__tests__/engine.integration.test.ts).

# @0xintuition/atom-parser

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/atom-parser

Applies to V2 · `@0xintuition/atom-parser` 0.1.0

## What it's for

Detect and normalize IIDs, text, JSON objects and arrays, URLs, IPFS URIs, addresses, names, and ISBNs into a `ParseResult`. Parsing identifies the input's shape; it does not resolve the entity, assign a canonical classification, or create an atom on-chain.

## When to use it

Use local detection before choosing a classification plugin or asking a reader to confirm an input. Set `remoteFetch: false` for local processing. URL and IPFS inspection is enabled by default, so a parser call is not inherently offline.

## Install

```sh
npm install @0xintuition/atom-parser@0.1.0
```

Use ESM with Node 22+ or Bun for the complete parser workflow.

## Entry points

| Subpath | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `.` | Parser, local detection, IID candidates, remote inspection, and types |
| `./types` | Parse results, options, remote outcomes, and `ParseError` |
| `./detect` | Local input detection |
| `./remote` | Bounded remote inspection and content detection |
| `./parse` | `parseAtom` entry point |
| `./iid` | Inspect IID-shaped candidates |
| `./ssrf` | Destination checks and pinned HTTP transport contracts |
| `./testing/dns` | Inject DNS behavior for isolated tests |

## Depends on and works with

Runtime package dependency: [iid](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/iid). Peer dependencies: none. The runtime dependency graph lists Intuition packages; the package manifest additionally declares `multiformats` and `viem` as ordinary dependencies.

Pass parsed evidence into an explicitly configured [classification engine](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/atom-classification). A structured-document candidate can contain schema types and URL hints, but those hints are not a persisted classification.

## @0xintuition/atom-parser - Example

This bounded fixed URL is normalized without fetching a page. Narrow on `kind` before reading variant-specific fields.

```ts
import { parseAtom, ParseError } from '@0xintuition/atom-parser';

export const parsed = await parseAtom('https://example.com/catalog', {
  remoteFetch: false,
  maxInputBytes: 1024,
});
if (parsed.kind === 'url') {
  console.log(parsed.canonicalUrl, parsed.remote === undefined);
}

try {
  await parseAtom('', { remoteFetch: false });
} catch (error) {
  if (!(error instanceof ParseError)) throw error;
  console.log(error.code);
}
```

The URL has no `remote` result, and empty input throws `ParseError` with code `EMPTY_INPUT`. Other input errors include `INPUT_TOO_LARGE` and invalid gateway configuration. `parseIidCandidate` returns `undefined` for non-IID input; an invalid IID-shaped candidate has `valid: false`, a reason, and no canonical IID. Detection is not proof that an identifier belongs to a particular entity.

Default limits are 16,384 input bytes, three redirects, 1 MiB response bytes, and 256 KiB inspected bytes. The request deadline is five seconds, or eight for IPFS; `connectTimeoutMs` does not enforce a separate connection deadline. IPFS inspection requires an explicit gateway. Remote outcomes include success, skipped, denied, timeout, error, oversized, and redirect-limit exhaustion; inspect warnings and the outcome before using remote evidence.

The pinned Node transport resolves and vets destinations, pins the approved address, and repeats checks on redirects. The older transport paragraph in the README does not describe this implementation; the linked source and transport test do. A custom transport must preserve the pinned-request contract, and your host still owns egress controls.

## Related concepts

[Representation profiles](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/representation-profiles) explains how identity becomes atom bytes. [Classify and enrich atoms](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/classify-enrich) continues from detection to meaning and provider artifacts.

## Source

[Package README](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/atom-parser/README.md), [public parser](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/atom-parser/src/parse.ts), and [pinned-transport test](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/atom-parser/__tests__/pinned-transport.test.ts).

# @0xintuition/atom-runtime

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/atom-runtime

Applies to V2 · `@0xintuition/atom-runtime` 0.1.0

## What it's for

A server composition layer for classification and enrichment engines, shared caches, presets, and configuration fingerprints. It does not provide graph storage, worker scheduling, or an automatically offline pipeline.

## When to use it

Use one runtime per intended configuration and application lifecycle to reuse engines and caches. Use the individual parser, classification, or enrichment packages for a single stage. Supplying no graph database removes a persistence prerequisite; it does not prevent selected providers from making requests.

## Install

```sh
npm install @0xintuition/atom-runtime@0.1.0
```

Use ESM and Promises on Node 20 or newer.

## Entry points

| Subpath | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `.` | Runtime/cache factories, configuration, presets, and consumer adapters |
| `./presets` | Classification plugins, enrichment factories, and default scopes |
| `./fingerprint` | Compute configuration identity |
| `./consumers` | Atom-services and local application composition adapters |
| `./config` | Resolve configuration and select processing environment keys |
| `./adapters/upstash` | Explicit HTTP cache integration |

## Depends on and works with

Runtime package dependencies: [atom-classification](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/atom-classification), [atom-enrichment](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/atom-enrichment), [atom-parser](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/atom-parser), [iid-registry](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/iid-registry), and [pipeline-runtime](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/pipeline-runtime). Peer dependencies: none. `zod` is an additional ordinary dependency in the package manifest.

Your host supplies transport, credentials, clock, logging, and persistent storage. Cache providers are `none`, `memory`, and `upstash`; inspect `cacheProvider` and `warnings` after resolution. Consumer adapters have their own cache defaults and fallback policies.

## @0xintuition/atom-runtime - Example

This runtime selects only deterministic text classifiers, an empty default enrichment set, a fixed clock, and memory caching. It performs one classification and proves that repeated engine lookup returns the same instance.

```ts
import {
  createPlainTextPlugin,
  createTypeProfilesPlugin,
} from '@0xintuition/atom-classification';
import { createProcessingRuntime } from '@0xintuition/atom-runtime';

export const runtime = createProcessingRuntime({
  config: { env: {}, cache: { provider: 'memory', memoryMaxEntries: 100 } },
  runtime: { now: () => '2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z' },
  overrides: {
    classification: [createTypeProfilesPlugin(), createPlainTextPlugin()],
    enrichment: { default: [] },
  },
});
try {
  const engine = runtime.classification.engine();
  const result = await engine.classify({
    input: 'A synthetic catalog idea',
    mode: 'client-only',
    classificationSessionId: 'runtime-reference',
  });
  console.log(engine === runtime.classification.engine());
  console.log(result.resolved?.publishable[0]?.type);
  console.log(runtime.cacheProvider, runtime.warnings);
} finally {
  runtime.dispose();
}
```

`runtime.fetch` in the composition options configures HTTP cache access; it is not a universal override for provider requests. Configure provider transports in their own options, or inject selected plugins as shown. Enrichment engines are memoized by preset and identity capability, and their published plugin registries are immutable. Change plugin selection when constructing the runtime.

Fingerprints include secret presence rather than secret values. They identify configuration, not the resulting entity or a persisted atom. Pass an explicit `env` map; only named `FromEnv` helpers read the process environment when called.

After `dispose()`, new engine lookups throw. Disposal does not cancel requests already in flight or revoke engine references already obtained. Supply and abort request signals before disposing when shutting down active work. The host owns retries and queues.

## Related concepts

[How the pieces fit](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/get-started/how-it-fits) locates this composition layer. [Classify and enrich atoms](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/classify-enrich) explains stage inputs and outputs; [Write a classification plugin](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/core/classification-plugin) explains the separate Core wiring required in a fork.

## Source

[Package README](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/atom-runtime/README.md), [runtime implementation](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/atom-runtime/src/runtime.ts), and [public runtime tests](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/atom-runtime/__tests__/public-runtime.test.ts).

# @0xintuition/classifications

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/classifications

Applies to V2 · `@0xintuition/classifications` 0.1.0

## What it's for

Canonical classification specifications define entity types, recommended fields, identity ladders, and relationship metadata. Creation Profiles package the field labels, schema provenance, predicate IDs, and allowed object targets needed to model a creation form.

## When to use it

Use `/creation/<slug>` for a known creation flow; use root registry helpers for dynamic discovery and validation. A classification slug (`music-recording`), schema type (`MusicRecording`), and display label are different values. Use [primitives](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/primitives) for identifier-first atom bytes and IDs; filling a field or selecting a relationship never submits a transaction or creates an edge.

## Install

```sh
npm install @0xintuition/classifications@0.1.0 viem@2.31.4
```

Use ESM imports. See [installation and peer setup](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/install).

## Entry points

| Subpath        | Purpose                                                                                                             |
| -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `.`            | Classification discovery, field validation, atom-data builders, identity derivation, and metadata predicate matrix. |
| `./*`          | Generated classification specs by slug, such as `/music-recording`.                                                 |
| `./creation`   | Generated Creation Profile registry.                                                                                |
| `./creation/*` | One generated Creation Profile by slug, such as `/creation/music-recording`.                                        |

## Depends on and works with

Runtime dependencies: [`@0xintuition/iid`](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/iid).

Published peers: `viem ^2.0.0`.

## @0xintuition/classifications - Example

```ts
import {
  buildAtomData,
  validateClassificationValues,
} from '@0xintuition/classifications';
import { musicRecordingCreationProfile } from '@0xintuition/classifications/creation/music-recording';

const recordingValues = {
  name: 'Example recording',
  byArtist: 'Example artist',
};
const issues = validateClassificationValues('music-recording', recordingValues);
if (issues.length > 0) {
  throw new Error(issues.map((issue) => issue.message).join('; '));
}
const recordingData = buildAtomData('music-recording', recordingValues);
const artistRelationship = musicRecordingCreationProfile.relationships.find(
  (relationship) => relationship.predicate.key === 'byArtist',
);
console.log({
  data: recordingData,
  fields: musicRecordingCreationProfile.fields.map((field) => field.key),
  artistTargets: artistRelationship?.expectedObjects,
});
```

These are synthetic descriptive values. `recordingData` contains a `byArtist` string; a graph assertion still needs a separate subject → predicate → object triple. `artistRelationship.expectedObjects` suggests `music-group` or `person` targets; it does not resolve an artist or create that target.

`validateClassificationValues` returns field issues for known classifications; an unknown slug throws. `buildAtomData` throws on invalid values. `getClassificationByReference` resolves trimmed, case-insensitive references through ordered lookup tiers; an ambiguous tier falls through and an unresolved reference returns `undefined`. A matching label is not evidence that two real-world entities are identical.

## Related concepts

See the [concept map](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts), [Build creation forms](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/creation-profiles), and [music catalog](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/examples/music-catalog).

## Source

[Package README at the pinned release](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/classifications/README.md).

[Creation Profile types](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/classifications/src/creation-profile.ts) · [Recording profile](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/classifications/src/generated/creation/music-recording.ts) · [Validation and serialization](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/classifications/src/atom-data.ts).

# @0xintuition/cli

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/cli

Applies to V2 · `@0xintuition/cli` 0.1.0

## What it's for

An `intuition` executable for encoder discovery and deterministic calldata generation, plus library exports for encoders and compatibility plan aliases. It does not own public clients, wallets, simulation, or submission.

## When to use it

Use it when a script or agent needs to discover an encoder or prepare a specific contract call. Use [SDK actions](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/sdk) for new action-envelope integrations. The executable has no plan command; its library's deprecated `build*Plan` aliases delegate to SDK-owned envelope builders.

## Install

```sh
npm install @0xintuition/cli@0.1.0
```

Use Node 20+ and ESM for library imports. The executable bundles its protocol, periphery, and SDK code; published types still reference those dependency APIs.

## Entry points

| Subpath | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `.` | Calldata encoders, envelope schemas, and deprecated plan aliases |

The `intuition` binary is a package executable, not an additional import subpath.

## Depends on and works with

Runtime package dependencies: [periphery](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/periphery), [protocol](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/protocol), and [sdk](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/sdk). Peer dependencies: none. `viem` is an ordinary runtime dependency in the package manifest.

An external executor owns deployment compatibility, fresh reads, simulation, approval, and signing. Envelope metadata identifies the SDK as the builder even when called through a deprecated CLI alias.

## @0xintuition/cli - Example

Discover core MultiVault write encoders using the exact package pin:

```sh
npx @0xintuition/cli@0.1.0 encoders list --surface core --contract multivault --kind write --json
```

The command prints the encoder catalog and does not submit a transaction. For `encode`, `--args` must be a JSON array; pass ABI integers as decimal strings to avoid JavaScript number precision loss. Invalid command arguments or unsupported encoders fail instead of producing a usable call.

Target support is contract-specific. Core targets cover the relevant Intuition mainnet/testnet and Base/Base Sepolia contracts; this does not make every contract available on every chain. Canonical bridge targets are mainnet-only, and the router lookup throws while a compatible redeployment is absent from the pinned map. FeeProxy and dynamic-fee curve intents carry explicit addresses and accept Intuition mainnet or testnet; accepting a chain ID does not prove deployment capability.

Review [action plans](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/action-plans) before handing encoded output to an executor. Encoding is neither execution authorization nor a successful simulation.

## Related concepts

[Protocol writes](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/protocol-writes) separates preparation, approval, and execution.

## Source

[Package README](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/cli/README.md), [network support matrix](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/cli/docs/network-support-matrix.md), and [executable source](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/tree/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/cli/src/bin).

# @0xintuition/curves

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/curves

Applies to V2 · `@0xintuition/curves` 0.1.0

## What it's for

Pure math for linear, progressive, and offset-progressive curves, fee calculations, and dynamic-fee distributions. It computes from supplied state and parameters without RPC, wallets, or deployment selection.

## When to use it

Use it for local previews or calculations from a known state snapshot. Use [protocol](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/protocol) or [SDK actions](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/sdk) when you need live contract state. A mathematically valid quote does not prove that a deployment uses those parameters or will execute at that price.

## Install

```sh
npm install @0xintuition/curves@0.1.0
```

Use ESM on Node 20+ or a compatible browser with BigInt support.

## Entry points

| Subpath | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `.` | Curve factories, conversions, previews, fees, distributions, math, and types |

Source module names such as `linear-curve` and `fees` are not public import subpaths.

## Depends on and works with

Runtime package dependencies: none. Peer dependencies: none.

The SDK consumes these calculations. Supply compatible current curve configuration, fees, and state from the intended contract; pure math has no way to establish their provenance.

## @0xintuition/curves - Example

This synthetic state has three asset base units and two share base units. Integer deposit conversion rounds down, while minting an exact number of shares rounds the required assets up.

```ts
import { createLinearCurve, type CurveState } from '@0xintuition/curves';

const curve = createLinearCurve();
const state: CurveState = { totalAssets: 3n, totalShares: 2n };
export const preview = {
  depositShares: curve.previewDeposit(2n, state),
  mintAssets: curve.previewMint(2n, state),
};
console.log(preview); // 1n share for a deposit; 3n assets to mint 2n shares.
```

Use `bigint` base units throughout. The example's `2n` means two base units, not two TRUST. `WAD` is the package's fixed-point scale of 10 to the power of 18; fee rates use the supplied denominator or the specific helper's basis-point contract. Avoid converting large values through JavaScript `number`.

Linear deposit and redeem previews round down; mint and withdraw previews round up. Invalid states can throw, such as nonzero shares with zero assets when converting assets to shares. These local previews exclude transaction gas and any fees you have not explicitly included.

Fee helpers include exact-net gross-up for atom/triple creation and deposits. The bounded search returns a quote achieving the requested net amount, but independently rounded fees can permit multiple solutions, so it does not promise the smallest gross debit. Dynamic-fee helpers require current lots, tier occupancy, configuration, and accumulators as applicable; the top tier's unbounded edge and width are `null`.

## Related concepts

[Protocol writes](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/protocol-writes) explains where a quote becomes a reviewed transaction. [How the pieces fit](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/get-started/how-it-fits) distinguishes pure helpers from live contract operations.

## Source

[Package README](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/curves/README.md), [linear math](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/curves/src/linear-curve.ts), and [fee helpers](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/curves/src/fees.ts).

# @0xintuition/deployments

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/deployments

Applies to V2 · `@0xintuition/deployments` 0.1.0

## What it's for

The shared source of contract ABIs, deployment addresses, chain definitions, and bytecode consumed by the protocol packages. Address selection is a local lookup; it does not query or deploy a contract.

## When to use it

Use it when you need metadata without the protocol wrapper layer. Use [protocol](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/protocol) for contract operations. A configured address proves that the pinned map contains an entry, not that its live implementation has a particular capability.

## Install

```sh
npm install @0xintuition/deployments@0.1.0 viem@2.31.4
```

Use ESM on Node 20+ or a compatible browser.

## Entry points

| Subpath | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `.` | Contract ABIs, address maps, chain definitions, and lookup helpers |
| `./bytecode` | Separate contract bytecode exports |

Bytecode stays off the root entry point so address and ABI consumers need not include it.

## Depends on and works with

Runtime package dependencies: none. Peer dependency: `viem ^2.0.0`.

Protocol, periphery, SDK, CLI, and React integrations share this metadata. Core and periphery address maps have different supported contract/chain combinations. The named Intuition chain definitions describe mainnet and testnet; Base and Base Sepolia addresses appear for applicable Base-side contracts.

## @0xintuition/deployments - Example

Select the testnet chain and its pinned MultiVault entry without a request:

```ts
import {
  getMultiVaultAddressFromChainId,
  intuitionTestnet,
} from '@0xintuition/deployments';

export const target = {
  chainId: intuitionTestnet.id,
  address: getMultiVaultAddressFromChainId(intuitionTestnet.id),
};
console.log(target);
```

`getContractAddressFromChainId` and the named core helpers throw when neither an override nor the canonical table supplies an address. Core helpers accept optional `AddressOverrides`; keep overrides specific to the intended deployment. This example reports metadata only, with no claim of a live testnet receipt or current deployment validation.

ABIs and bytecode have distinct uses. Metalayer `MetaERC20Hub`, `MetaERC20Spoke`, and `MetaNativeSpoke` bytecode exports contain deployed runtime code, not creation code. `MultiVaultBytecode` contains an unresolved library link placeholder; link it with the matching contract build's references before any deployment. Do not treat every bytecode export as ready to deploy.

## Related concepts

[Protocol writes](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/protocol-writes) explains why an action needs both a chain and a compatible target.

## Source

[Package README](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/deployments/README.md), [lookup helpers](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/deployments/src/helpers.ts), and [contract artifact provenance](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/docs/contract-artifacts.md).

# @0xintuition/ids

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/ids

Applies to V2 · `@0xintuition/ids` 0.1.0

## What it's for

IDs computes deterministic protocol atom, predicate, triple, and counter-triple IDs. The result identifies exact bytes or ordered components; it does not determine whether two descriptions refer to the same real-world entity.

## When to use it

Use it when bytes or component IDs are already known. Use [iid](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/iid) for entity identifier grammar and [primitives](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/primitives) for validated construction. Calculating an ID neither registers an atom nor submits a transaction.

## Install

```sh
npm install @0xintuition/ids@0.1.0 viem@2.31.4
```

Use ESM imports. See [installation and peer setup](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/install).

## Entry points

| Subpath | Purpose                                                                                                              |
| ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `.`     | Atom, predicate, triple, counter-triple, OAuth and auth-user hashes; salts, hash validation, and formatting helpers. |

## Depends on and works with

Runtime dependencies: none.

Published peers: `viem ^2.0.0`.

## @0xintuition/ids - Example

```ts
import {
  calculateAtomId,
  calculateCounterTripleId,
  calculateTripleId,
} from '@0xintuition/ids';
import { toHex } from 'viem';

// Synthetic bytes, with no claim about a real recording or artist.
const data = 'example:recording';
const recordingId = calculateAtomId(data);
const artistId = calculateAtomId('example:artist');
const predicateId = calculateAtomId('example:relationship');
const tripleId = calculateTripleId(recordingId, predicateId, artistId);
const reverseId = calculateTripleId(artistId, predicateId, recordingId);
const counterId = calculateCounterTripleId(tripleId);
console.log({
  sameBytes: recordingId === calculateAtomId(toHex(data)),
  changedBytes: recordingId !== calculateAtomId(`${data} `),
  reverseDiffers: reverseId !== tripleId,
  counterDiffersFromReverse: counterId.toString() !== reverseId.toString(),
});
```

`calculateAtomId` accepts a UTF-8 string or hex-encoded bytes. A hex-looking input is treated as bytes, so encode explicitly with `toHex` when the intended data is the literal text `0x...`. A trailing space changes the payload and therefore its atom ID.

Triple hashing uses **subject, predicate, object** in that order. A reversed triple makes a different assertion; a counter-triple instead derives from the original triple ID to identify its negation. Neither operation merges identities. Authentication-related hashes are deterministic public identifiers, not encryption for secrets.

## Related concepts

See the [concept map](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts) and [Representation profiles](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/representation-profiles) for the difference between entity identity and payload identity.

## Source

[Package README at the pinned release](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/ids/README.md).

[Atom hashing](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/ids/src/atom-id.ts) · [Ordered triple and counter-triple hashing](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/ids/src/triple-id.ts).

# @0xintuition/iid-ladder

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/iid-ladder

Applies to V2 · `@0xintuition/iid-ladder` 0.1.0

## What it's for

The projection ladder selects a primary IID from supplied strong identifiers, provider handles, and canonical URLs. If nothing usable is available, it returns an explicit envelope fallback with a null IID.

## When to use it

Use it before atom construction when imports contain several candidate identifiers. The selection order is strong identifier → registered provider handle → canonical URL → envelope fallback. It does not search by name, prove a unique entity match, serialize atom bytes, record aliases, or fetch provider metadata.

## Install

```sh
npm install @0xintuition/iid-ladder@0.1.0
```

Use ESM imports. See [installation and peer setup](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/install).

## Entry points

| Subpath | Purpose                                                                                                                        |
| ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `.`     | Identifier projection, category ordering, matching aliases, bound policy creation, and pinned Wikidata classification helpers. |

## Depends on and works with

Runtime dependencies: [`@0xintuition/iid`](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/iid).

Published peers: none.

## @0xintuition/iid-ladder - Example

```ts
import { projectIdentifierLadder } from '@0xintuition/iid-ladder';

const selection = projectIdentifierLadder({
  strongIdentifiers: { isrc: 'US-RC1-76-07839' },
  canonicalUrl: 'https://example.com/recording',
});
if (selection.iid === null) {
  console.log({ needsIdentityEvidence: true, reason: selection.reason });
} else {
  console.log({ iid: selection.iid, selectedFrom: selection.rung });
}
const noIdentifier = projectIdentifierLadder({});
console.log(noIdentifier);
```

The supplied strong ISRC wins over the URL. Empty input returns `iid: null`; inspect `reason` and collect more evidence or use an explicit envelope. A name-only recipe belongs to the declarative IID engine and a classification ladder; identical names can describe different entities.

`strongIdentifierOrder` is an allowlist as well as an order. Category policies distinguish primary identities from aliases used only for matching. Default `providerLocalHandles: 'reject'` leaves unregistered provider namespaces as fallbacks. The optional `'mint'` policy preserves application-local historical strings; it does not make them canonical registered IIDs or P0-eligible. Package-specific identifier additions are disclosed on the [specification page](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/iid-spec).

## Related concepts

Read [Representation profiles](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/representation-profiles), then [Primitives](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/primitives) to turn a selected identity into bytes.

## Source

[Package README at the pinned release](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/iid-ladder/README.md).

[Canonical identity ladders](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-identifier/blob/3e593247c0e7cb168b37368937167ed146d3868a/spec/05-identity-ladders.md) · [Canonical gen1 derivation](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-identifier/blob/3e593247c0e7cb168b37368937167ed146d3868a/spec/06-gen1.md) · [Projection implementation](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/iid-ladder/src/ladder.ts).

# @0xintuition/iid-registry

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/iid-registry

Applies to V2 · `@0xintuition/iid-registry` 0.1.0

## What it's for

The registry maps identifier schemes and values to known classifications, provider capability names, and provider hints. These are pure local lookups, not fetched provider responses.

## When to use it

Use it when a parsed identifier needs semantic meaning or an enrichment plan. A provider name does not mean its client is installed, credentials are available, or a match exists. Use [atom-enrichment](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/atom-enrichment) for provider execution; no HTTP request, cache, or credential handling happens here.

## Install

```sh
npm install @0xintuition/iid-registry@0.1.0 viem@2.31.4
```

Use ESM imports. See [installation and peer setup](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/install).

## Entry points

| Subpath | Purpose                                                                                         |
| ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `.`     | Classification lookups, ordered provider plans, provider names, and typed identifier-hint maps. |

## Depends on and works with

Runtime dependencies: [`@0xintuition/classifications`](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/classifications), [`@0xintuition/iid`](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/iid).

Published peers: `viem ^2.0.0`.

## @0xintuition/iid-registry - Example

```ts
import {
  classificationForIid,
  identifierHintsForIid,
  providersForIid,
} from '@0xintuition/iid-registry';

const inputIid = 'int:isrc:USRC17607839';
const classification = classificationForIid(inputIid);
const providerPlan = providersForIid(inputIid);
const hints = identifierHintsForIid(inputIid);
const unmapped = classificationForIid('int:iswc:T0345246801');
console.log({ classification, providerPlan, hints, unmapped });
```

The ISRC maps to `music-recording`, and its plan lists `musicbrainz`, `spotify`, and `apple-music` capabilities in that order. The example performs no search and returns no recording metadata. The valid ISWC example has no mapped classification: the registry has no music-composition classification.

An empty provider plan does not make an IID invalid. Bare polymorphic values can also remain unclassified. Historical spellings that can be canonicalized may resolve through their canonical form; that does not make those spellings eligible new anchors.

## Related concepts

See the [concept map](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts) and [Classify and enrich atoms](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/classify-enrich).

## Source

[Package README at the pinned release](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/iid-registry/README.md).

[Canonical registry governance](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-identifier/blob/3e593247c0e7cb168b37368937167ed146d3868a/spec/09-registry-governance.md) · [Canonical scheme registry](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-identifier/blob/3e593247c0e7cb168b37368937167ed146d3868a/registry.json) · [Classification mapping](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/iid-registry/src/classification.ts) · [Provider plans](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/iid-registry/src/providers.ts).

# @0xintuition/iid-spec

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/iid-spec

Applies to V2 · `@0xintuition/iid-spec` 0.1.0

## What it's for

This package distributes IID specification documents and machine-readable conformance fixtures. It has no JavaScript runtime API; the canonical authority for these docs is the separate Intuition Identifier specification.

## When to use it

Use the documents and fixtures to implement or compare identifier producers. Use [iid](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/iid) for application parsing and derivation, and [iid-registry](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/iid-registry) for classification and provider planning. The packaged copy differs from the canonical source, so a package fixture alone does not establish canonical-spec conformance.

## Install

```sh
npm install @0xintuition/iid-spec@0.1.0
```

The JSON artifacts can be read from Node; there is no root runtime export.

## Entry points

| Subpath                | Purpose                                                                                                                     |
| ---------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `./conformance/*.json` | Machine-readable fixture documents, including canonicalization, parsing, validation, normalization, and derivation vectors. |

## Depends on and works with

Runtime dependencies: none.

Published peers: none.

## @0xintuition/iid-spec - Example

This Node example loads a published data artifact through its exported path; it does not invent a runtime import from the package root.

```ts
import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { createRequire } from 'node:module';

const require = createRequire(import.meta.url);
const vectorsPath = require.resolve(
  '@0xintuition/iid-spec/conformance/canonicalization.json',
);
const packagedVectors: unknown = JSON.parse(readFileSync(vectorsPath, 'utf8'));
console.log({ loadedConformanceDocument: typeof packagedVectors === 'object' });
```

For an independent implementation, compare against the canonical [registry](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-identifier/blob/3e593247c0e7cb168b37368937167ed146d3868a/registry.json) and [test vectors](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-identifier/blob/3e593247c0e7cb168b37368937167ed146d3868a/test-vectors.json) as well as the packaged corpus. Loading the file is not a conformance test.

The canonical specification is version 0.1.0. Its [representation profiles, including §7.8](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-identifier/blob/3e593247c0e7cb168b37368937167ed146d3868a/spec/07-representation-profiles.md), define identity data separately from companion metadata. The package copy lacks §7.8 and adds typed `wd` values, the weak `acct` form, and the `apple-podcasts`, `letterboxd`, and `podcast-index` schemes. Chapters 00, 01, 04, 05, and 09 also differ. These are package extensions or discrepancies, not silently adopted canonical rules; this is the open M-1 source mismatch.

## Related concepts

Read [Representation profiles](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/representation-profiles) for identity payloads versus companion context, then the [concept map](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts).

## Source

[Package README at the pinned release](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/iid-spec/README.md).

[Canonical specification](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-identifier/blob/3e593247c0e7cb168b37368937167ed146d3868a/spec/00-overview.md) · [Canonical registry governance](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-identifier/blob/3e593247c0e7cb168b37368937167ed146d3868a/spec/09-registry-governance.md) · [Packaged representation profiles](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/iid-spec/spec/07-representation-profiles.md).

# @0xintuition/iid

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/iid

Applies to V2 · `@0xintuition/iid` 0.1.0

## What it's for

IID implements identifier grammar, scheme canonicalization, normalization, recipe hashing, and declarative identity ladders. An IID names an entity; it is not the protocol atom ID of every representation of that entity.

## When to use it

Use `inspectIntuitionId` for a typed validity result and `SCHEMES` for explicit canonicalization. Use [ids](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/ids) to hash atom bytes, [primitives](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/primitives) to select a representation, and [iid-registry](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/iid-registry) for meaning and provider plans. Parsing or passing validation does not prove a record exists at an external registry.

## Install

```sh
npm install @0xintuition/iid@0.1.0 viem@2.31.4
```

Use ESM imports. See [installation and peer setup](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/install).

## Entry points

| Subpath | Purpose                                                                                                             |
| ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `.`     | Parsing, validation, inspection, scheme canonicalizers, NORM-1, gen1 derivation, and the declarative ladder engine. |

## Depends on and works with

Runtime dependencies: none.

Published peers: `viem ^2.0.0`.

## @0xintuition/iid - Example

```ts
import { inspectIntuitionId, SCHEMES } from '@0xintuition/iid';

const canonicalIsrc = SCHEMES.isrc.canonicalize('US-RC1-76-07839');
if (canonicalIsrc === undefined) throw new Error('Invalid ISRC');
const identifier = `int:isrc:${canonicalIsrc}`;
const inspection = inspectIntuitionId(identifier);
if (!inspection.valid) throw new Error(inspection.reason);
console.log({ iid: identifier, anchorEligible: inspection.anchorEligible });
```

This separate ISRC conformance example produces `int:isrc:USRC17607839`; it is not an identifier for the synthetic catalog recording. Canonicalization can return `undefined`. Inspection distinguishes a non-canonical spelling from an unknown or invalid scheme; a non-canonical result can offer a `canonical` value, but it is not a valid new anchor.

Validity and bare P0 eligibility are separate. Class C recipe-derived identifiers need P1 evidence. Bare polymorphic identifiers also require a typed envelope. The package implements additional identifier forms beyond the pinned canonical source; see the [specification differences](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/iid-spec).

## Related concepts

Read [Representation profiles](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/representation-profiles) and the [offline quickstart](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/get-started/quickstart).

## Source

[Package README at the pinned release](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/iid/README.md).

[Canonical grammar](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-identifier/blob/3e593247c0e7cb168b37368937167ed146d3868a/spec/02-grammar.md) · [Canonical normalization](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-identifier/blob/3e593247c0e7cb168b37368937167ed146d3868a/spec/04-normalization.md) · [Canonical representation profiles](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-identifier/blob/3e593247c0e7cb168b37368937167ed146d3868a/spec/07-representation-profiles.md) · [Inspection implementation](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/iid/src/parse.ts).

# Packages

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages

Applies to V2 · `@0xintuition/atom-classification` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/atom-enrichment` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/atom-parser` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/atom-runtime` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/classifications` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/cli` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/curves` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/deployments` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/ids` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/iid` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/iid-ladder` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/iid-registry` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/iid-spec` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/periphery` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/pipeline-runtime` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/predicates` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/primitives` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/protocol` 4.0.0 · `@0xintuition/react` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/schema-org` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/sdk` 4.0.0

These stable packages separate vocabulary, identity, local construction, processing, and protocol operations. Each reference lists its exact install pin, public entry points, runtime dependencies, and peers. Start with [installation](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/install) or the [offline quickstart](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/get-started/quickstart).

An atom ID identifies exact bytes; an IID names an entity; a triple explicitly relates three atom IDs. Local construction does not create on-chain terms. Indexed V2 graph reads use the [Query API of a Core node you run](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/query-core).
