## Using the reference

Amounts and shares use `bigint` base units. Term IDs are protocol IDs, not IID strings. Use each page’s public import paths; source directories do not add package entry points. Optional dependency parameters are customization and testing hooks. Quotes can become stale before execution.

Review [SDK packages](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/sdk), [Compatibility](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/compatibility), [the SDK read client](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/read-with-sdk), and [action envelopes](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/action-plans) before integrating.

# MultiVault actions

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/sdk/multivault

Applies to V2 · `@0xintuition/sdk` 4.0.0

API for `@0xintuition/sdk@4.0.0`. [Compatibility](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/compatibility) · [Source](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/sdk/src/actions/multivault.ts).

Import from `@0xintuition/sdk/actions`.

Signatures show the exact accepted inputs and return types. Named input/output structures and dependency-injection types are listed below; viem and protocol types come from their respective packages. Preparation and quote functions can perform RPC reads. Envelope builders on the action-envelope pages use caller-supplied read context and perform no RPC reads or signing. **`feeProxyExecutePlan` sends transactions**; the other SDK actions on these pages prepare transactions or read data.

## multivaultResolveDepositFeeBase

Resolves the base MultiVault will charge fees on for a deposit.

On a vault's first deposit MultiVault nets a min-share bootstrap cost out of the gross assets
BEFORE computing any fee (doubled for triples) — see `MultiVaultLib._calculateAtomDeposit`. A quote
that applies fee rates to the gross amount therefore disagrees with the contract on exactly that
deposit, in every fee component at once. Exported because more than one quote needs it, and
because a consumer reconciling a quote against a receipt needs to know which number was quoted.

[Source](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/sdk/src/actions/multivault.ts#L498)

```ts
function multivaultResolveDepositFeeBase(
  config: ReadConfig,
  inputs: {
    termId: Hex;
    curveId: bigint;
    assetsIn: bigint;
  },
  deps?: MultiVaultDepositFeeBaseDeps,
): Promise<MultiVaultDepositFeeBase>;
```

- **`config`**: MultiVault address and public client.
- **`inputs`**: The term, curve and gross assets being deposited.
- **returns**: The fee base, whether this is the bootstrapping deposit, and what the bootstrap cost.

Defaults: `deps = defaultDepositFeeBaseDeps`. Dependency arguments are optional test/customization hooks; normal consumers use the built-in dependencies.

## multivaultQuoteTermDepositFee

The term-type-specific deposit fee: the atom-wallet cut on an atom, or the underlying-atom
fraction on a triple.

MultiVault charges this alongside its entry and protocol fees, so a quote that reports only those
two can never sum to the shares actually minted. On an atom it is `atomWalletDepositFee` applied
to the fee base; on a triple it is `atomDepositFractionForTriple`, waived unless ALL THREE
underlying atoms are individually above the fee threshold.

[Source](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/sdk/src/actions/multivault.ts#L545)

```ts
function multivaultQuoteTermDepositFee(
  config: ReadConfig,
  inputs: {
    termId: Hex;
    feeBaseAssets: bigint;
  },
  deps?: MultiVaultDepositFeeBaseDeps & MultiVaultTermFeeDeps,
): Promise<{
  kind: 'atom-wallet' | 'atom-deposit-fraction';
  fee: bigint;
  waived: boolean;
}>;
```

- **`config`**: MultiVault address and public client.
- **`inputs`**: The term and the fee base to charge on.
- **`deps`**: Injectable protocol read primitives.
- **returns**: The fee and which kind it is.

Defaults: `deps = {
		...defaultDepositFeeBaseDeps,
		...defaultTermFeeDeps,
	}`. Dependency arguments are optional test/customization hooks; normal consumers use the built-in dependencies.

## multivaultWillChargeEntryFee

Whether MultiVault will charge its entry fee on a deposit into this term.

Waived while the DEFAULT curve's vault holds fewer shares than `feeThreshold`: fees are routed
into that vault, and donating them into a near-empty share supply would move its price. A quote
that assumes the fee always applies overstates it.

[Source](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/sdk/src/actions/multivault.ts#L600)

```ts
function multivaultWillChargeEntryFee(
  config: ReadConfig,
  inputs: {
    termId: Hex;
  },
  deps?: MultiVaultFeeContextDeps,
): Promise<boolean>;
```

- **`config`**: MultiVault address and public client.
- **`inputs`**: The term being deposited into.
- **returns**: True if the entry fee applies.

Defaults: `deps = defaultFeeContextDeps`. Dependency arguments are optional test/customization hooks; normal consumers use the built-in dependencies.

## multivaultWillChargeExitFee

Whether MultiVault will charge its exit fee on a redemption.

Same threshold as the entry fee, measured on what the default vault would be LEFT with — so
whether it applies depends on the size of the redemption, not only on the term.

[Source](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/sdk/src/actions/multivault.ts#L625)

```ts
function multivaultWillChargeExitFee(
  config: ReadConfig,
  inputs: {
    termId: Hex;
    curveId: bigint;
    sharesIn: bigint;
  },
  deps?: MultiVaultFeeContextDeps,
): Promise<boolean>;
```

- **`config`**: MultiVault address and public client.
- **`inputs`**: The term, curve and share count being redeemed.
- **returns**: True if the exit fee applies.

Defaults: `deps = defaultFeeContextDeps`. Dependency arguments are optional test/customization hooks; normal consumers use the built-in dependencies.

## multivaultQuoteCurveRedeemFee

The curve-level withdrawal fee for a specific account, or zero if the curve charges none.

Curve-agnostic: it asks the curve whether it has a redeem hook and, if so, quotes it for THIS
account. MultiVault's own `previewRedeem` quotes the same hook with the zero address, which on a
curve whose rate keys on the holder's entry tier is a different — and for a slippage floor,
unusable — number.

[Source](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/sdk/src/actions/multivault.ts#L655)

```ts
function multivaultQuoteCurveRedeemFee(
  config: ReadConfig,
  inputs: {
    termId: Hex;
    curveId: bigint;
    account: Address;
    assetsBeforeFees: bigint;
  },
  deps?: MultiVaultCurveRedeemFeeDeps,
): Promise<{
  curveAddress: Address | null;
  curveFee: bigint;
}>;
```

- **`config`**: MultiVault address and public client.
- **`inputs`**: The term, curve, redeeming account and gross assets.
- **returns**: The curve's withdrawal fee for that account, and the curve it was quoted from.

Defaults: `deps = defaultCurveRedeemFeeDeps`. Dependency arguments are optional test/customization hooks; normal consumers use the built-in dependencies.

## multivaultQuoteDepositPlan

Read current vault and fee state and return a deposit quote, including expected output and the minimum shares to accept. No transaction is sent.

[Source](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/sdk/src/actions/multivault.ts#L676)

```ts
function multivaultQuoteDepositPlan(
  config: ReadConfig,
  inputs: {
    termId: Hex;
    curveId: bigint;
    assetsIn: bigint;
    slippageBps?: bigint;
  },
  deps?: MultiVaultQuoteDeps,
): Promise<MultiVaultDepositQuotePlan>;
```

Defaults: `deps = defaultQuoteDeps`. Dependency arguments are optional test/customization hooks; normal consumers use the built-in dependencies.

## multivaultPrepareDepositTx

Prepares a deposit transaction sized against its own quote.

MultiVault deposits exactly `msg.value`, so the transaction value IS the deposit: it defaults to
`assetsIn`, the amount the quote and its slippage floor were computed for. An explicit `value`
is passed through as given.

[Source](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/sdk/src/actions/multivault.ts#L757)

```ts
function multivaultPrepareDepositTx(
  config: WriteConfig,
  inputs: {
    receiver: Address;
    termId: Hex;
    curveId: bigint;
    assetsIn: bigint;
    slippageBps?: bigint;
    value?: bigint;
  },
  deps?: MultiVaultQuoteDeps,
): Promise<MultiVaultPrepareDepositTxResult>;
```

- **`config`**: MultiVault address and viem clients.
- **`inputs`**: Receiver, term, curve, gross assets, optional slippage and optional explicit value.
- **`deps`**: Injectable protocol read primitives.
- **returns**: The deposit calldata, args, the value to send with it, and the quote it was built from.

Defaults: `deps = defaultQuoteDeps`. Dependency arguments are optional test/customization hooks; normal consumers use the built-in dependencies.

## multivaultGetUserPositionSnapshot

Read an account balance and vault state for one term/curve pair and return its current position snapshot.

[Source](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/sdk/src/actions/multivault.ts#L788)

```ts
function multivaultGetUserPositionSnapshot(
  config: ReadConfig,
  inputs: {
    account: Address;
    termId: Hex;
    curveId: bigint;
    includeUtilization?: boolean;
  },
  deps?: MultiVaultPositionDeps,
): Promise<MultiVaultUserPositionSnapshot>;
```

Defaults: `deps = defaultPositionDeps`. Dependency arguments are optional test/customization hooks; normal consumers use the built-in dependencies.

## multivaultQuoteRedeemPlan

Quotes what a SPECIFIC account receives for redeeming shares, and the floor to send with it.

`account` is required, and that is the point. MultiVault's `previewRedeem` quotes any curve redeem
hook with the zero address, so on a curve whose withdrawal rate keys on where the holder entered
it returns a number that belongs to no one — and a `minAssets` derived from it is wrong in both
directions: too loose when it understates the payout, and unmeetable (the redeem reverts) when it
overstates it. This composes the payout from parts that each know who is asking: MultiVault's
gross conversion, its protocol fee, its exit fee where that fee actually applies, and the curve's
own account-aware quote.

[Source](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/sdk/src/actions/multivault.ts#L871)

```ts
function multivaultQuoteRedeemPlan(
  config: ReadConfig,
  inputs: {
    termId: Hex;
    curveId: bigint;
    account: Address;
    sharesIn: bigint;
    slippageBps?: bigint;
  },
  deps?: MultiVaultRedeemQuoteDeps,
): Promise<MultiVaultRedeemQuotePlan>;
```

- **`config`**: MultiVault address and public client.
- **`inputs`**: The term, curve, redeeming account, share count and optional slippage.
- **`deps`**: Injectable protocol read primitives.
- **returns**: The account's payout, its fee breakdown, and a slippage floor derived from it.

Defaults: `deps = defaultRedeemQuoteDeps`. Dependency arguments are optional test/customization hooks; normal consumers use the built-in dependencies.

## multivaultPrepareRedeemTx

Prepares a redeem transaction for a specific account, sized against its own quote.

[Source](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/sdk/src/actions/multivault.ts#L939)

```ts
function multivaultPrepareRedeemTx(
  config: WriteConfig,
  inputs: {
    receiver: Address;
    termId: Hex;
    curveId: bigint;
    account: Address;
    sharesIn: bigint;
    slippageBps?: bigint;
  },
  deps?: MultiVaultRedeemQuoteDeps,
): Promise<MultiVaultPrepareRedeemTxResult>;
```

- **`config`**: MultiVault address and viem clients.
- **`inputs`**: Receiver, term, curve, redeeming account, share count and optional slippage.
- **`deps`**: Injectable protocol read primitives.
- **returns**: The redeem calldata, args, and the quote it was built from.

Defaults: `deps = defaultRedeemQuoteDeps`. Dependency arguments are optional test/customization hooks; normal consumers use the built-in dependencies.

## multivaultCreateAndSeedTerm

function multivaultCreateAndSeedTerm(

): Promise<MultiVaultCreateAndSeedTermPlan>;
```

Defaults: `deps = defaultCreateAndSeedDeps`. Dependency arguments are optional test/customization hooks; normal consumers use the built-in dependencies.

## multivaultGetUtilizationAnalyticsBundle

Read protocol and personal utilization over the requested epochs and return an analytics bundle.

[Source](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/sdk/src/actions/multivault.ts#L1099)

## multivaultPrepareOnBehalfOfCreationPlan

Prepares an on-behalf-of creation plan: `createAtomsFor` / `createTriplesFor` require
`creator` to have granted `caller` CREATION approval first, so this reads that
approval state and — if missing — prepends the `approve` calldata as its own step.
The approval step and the creation steps have DIFFERENT required signers
(`creator` vs `caller`); the caller of this function is responsible for routing each
step to the right signer, in order.

[Source](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/sdk/src/actions/multivault.ts#L1247)

```ts
function multivaultPrepareOnBehalfOfCreationPlan(
  config: ReadConfig,
  inputs: {
    creator: Address;
    caller: Address;
    atoms?: MultiVaultOnBehalfOfAtomInput[];
    triples?: MultiVaultOnBehalfOfTripleInput[];
  },
  deps?: MultiVaultOnBehalfOfCreationDeps,
): Promise<MultiVaultOnBehalfOfCreationPlan>;
```

- **`config`**: Read config for MultiVault.
- **`inputs`**: The creator being created for, the caller acting on their behalf, and the atoms/triples to create.
- **`deps`**: Injectable protocol read primitives.
- **returns**: The ordered steps (approval, if needed, then creation) and whether approval was already in place.

Defaults: `deps = defaultOnBehalfOfCreationDeps`. Dependency arguments are optional test/customization hooks; normal consumers use the built-in dependencies.

## multivaultPrepareMulticallTx

Assembles a consolidated payable `multicall` batch: the `bytes[]` sub-call array and
the `uint256[]` per-sub-call value array must stay aligned and their values must sum
to exactly `msg.value` — the fiddliest part of building this call by hand.

[Source](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/sdk/src/actions/multivault.ts#L1339)

```ts
function multivaultPrepareMulticallTx(
  subCalls: MultiVaultMulticallSubCall[],
): MultiVaultPrepareMulticallTxResult;
```

- **`subCalls`**: The sub-calls to batch, each with its own calldata and value allocation.
- **returns**: The `multicall` calldata, args, and the total value the batch requires.

## Imported type provenance

Public import locations and the definitions used by these signatures and helper types. Value imports appear where a dependency hook uses `typeof`.

| Name in this module                     | Public import                                                                   | Definition                                                                                                                                                                              |

## Input and result types

Exported declarations are public imports from the SDK subpath above. Module-local helper aliases describe accepted shapes but are not public exports.

### PreviewDepositTuple

Module-local helper; not a public export.

```ts
type PreviewDepositTuple = readonly [bigint, bigint] & {
  shares?: bigint;
  assetsAfterFees?: bigint;
};
```

Module-local helper; not a public export.

```ts
type PreviewCreateTuple = readonly [bigint, bigint, bigint] & {
  shares?: bigint;
  feeBaseAssets?: bigint;
  assetsAfterFees?: bigint;
};
```

### MultiVaultDepositQuotePlan

Public export.

```ts
export type MultiVaultDepositQuotePlan = {
  termId: Hex;
  curveId: bigint;
  assetsIn: bigint;
  /** What every fee was actually charged on — `assetsIn` less any min-share bootstrap cost. */
  feeBaseAssets: bigint;
  minShareCost: bigint;
  isFirstDeposit: boolean;
  sharesOut: bigint;
  minSharesOut: bigint;
  assetsAfterFees: bigint;
  /** Zero when MultiVault waives it below `feeThreshold`. */
  entryFee: bigint;
  entryFeeWaived: boolean;
  protocolFee: bigint;
  /**
   * The term-type-specific fee charged alongside the other two: the atom-wallet cut on an atom,
   * the underlying-atom fraction on a triple. Without it the components cannot sum to the whole.
   */
  termFee: bigint;
  termFeeKind: 'atom-wallet' | 'atom-deposit-fraction';
  termFeeWaived: boolean;
  totalEstimatedFees: bigint;
  currentSharePrice: bigint;
  effectivePricePerShare: bigint | null;
  slippageBps: bigint;
};
```

### MultiVaultPrepareDepositTxResult

Public export.

```ts
export type MultiVaultPrepareDepositTxResult = {
  args: readonly [Address, Hex, bigint, bigint];
  calldata: Hex;
  /** The value to send: the deposit itself, `assetsIn` unless an explicit value was passed. */
  value: bigint;
  quote: MultiVaultDepositQuotePlan;
};
```

### MultiVaultRedeemQuotePlan

Public export.

```ts
export type MultiVaultRedeemQuotePlan = {
  termId: Hex;
  curveId: bigint;
  /** The account whose payout this is. A redeem quote is meaningless without one. */
  account: Address;
  sharesIn: bigint;
  sharesUsed: bigint;
  assetsBeforeFees: bigint;
  assetsOut: bigint;
  minAssetsOut: bigint;
  /** Zero when MultiVault waives it below `feeThreshold`. */
  exitFee: bigint;
  exitFeeWaived: boolean;
  protocolFee: bigint;
  /** The curve's own withdrawal fee for THIS account. Zero on a curve without a redeem hook. */
  curveFee: bigint;
  curveAddress: Address | null;
  totalEstimatedFees: bigint;
  currentSharePrice: bigint;
  effectivePricePerShare: bigint | null;
  slippageBps: bigint;
};
```

# Bridge action envelopes

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/sdk/plans-base

Applies to V2 · `@0xintuition/sdk` 4.0.0

API for `@0xintuition/sdk@4.0.0`. [Compatibility](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/compatibility) · [Source](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/sdk/src/actions/plans/base.ts).

Import from `@0xintuition/sdk/actions`.

Signatures show the exact accepted inputs and return types. Named input/output structures and dependency-injection types are listed below; viem and protocol types come from their respective packages. Preparation and quote functions can perform RPC reads. Envelope builders on the action-envelope pages use caller-supplied read context and perform no RPC reads or signing. **`feeProxyExecutePlan` sends transactions**; the other SDK actions on these pages prepare transactions or read data.

## baseTrustBridgeToIntuitionEnvelope

Encode approval and Base-to-Intuition TRUST bridge steps using supplied allowance and fee context, without RPC or signing.

[Source](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/sdk/src/actions/plans/base.ts#L80)

```ts
function baseTrustBridgeToIntuitionEnvelope(
  inputs: BuildBaseTrustBridgeToIntuitionPlanInputs,
): Promise<import('@0xintuition/sdk/actions').AgentActionEnvelope>;
```

## intuitionTrustBridgeToBaseEnvelope

Encode Intuition-to-Base TRUST bridge steps using supplied fee context, without RPC or signing.

[Source](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/sdk/src/actions/plans/base.ts#L162)

```ts
function intuitionTrustBridgeToBaseEnvelope(
  inputs: BuildIntuitionTrustBridgeToBasePlanInputs,
): Promise<import('@0xintuition/sdk/actions').AgentActionEnvelope>;
```

## baseERC20BridgeToIntuitionEnvelope

Encode ERC-20 approval and bridge steps from Base using supplied allowance and fee context.

[Source](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/sdk/src/actions/plans/base.ts#L220)

```ts
function baseERC20BridgeToIntuitionEnvelope(
  inputs: BuildBaseERC20BridgeToIntuitionPlanInputs,
): Promise<import('@0xintuition/sdk/actions').AgentActionEnvelope>;
```

## intuitionERC20BridgeToBaseEnvelope

Encode ERC-20 approval and bridge steps from Intuition using supplied allowance and fee context.

[Source](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/sdk/src/actions/plans/base.ts#L316)

```ts
function intuitionERC20BridgeToBaseEnvelope(
  inputs: BuildIntuitionERC20BridgeToBasePlanInputs,
): Promise<import('@0xintuition/sdk/actions').AgentActionEnvelope>;
```

## Imported type provenance

Public import locations and the definitions used by these signatures and helper types. Value imports appear where a dependency hook uses `typeof`.

# Dynamic-fee action envelopes

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/sdk/plans-dynamic-fee-curve

Applies to V2 · `@0xintuition/sdk` 4.0.0

API for `@0xintuition/sdk@4.0.0`. [Compatibility](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/compatibility) · [Source](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/sdk/src/actions/plans/dynamic-fee-curve.ts).

Import from `@0xintuition/sdk/actions`.

Signatures show the exact accepted inputs and return types. Named input/output structures and dependency-injection types are listed below; viem and protocol types come from their respective packages. Preparation and quote functions can perform RPC reads. Envelope builders on the action-envelope pages use caller-supplied read context and perform no RPC reads or signing. **`feeProxyExecutePlan` sends transactions**; the other SDK actions on these pages prepare transactions or read data.

## dynamicFeeCurveDepositEnvelope

Builds a deposit plan into a dynamic-fee vault: resolves the curve from the registry,
quotes the piecewise deposit fee (exact across every band traversed, not just the
pre-deposit tier), and returns the MultiVault `deposit` calldata sized against the
slippage-floored share quote.

[Source](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/sdk/src/actions/plans/dynamic-fee-curve.ts#L135)

```ts
function dynamicFeeCurveDepositEnvelope(
  inputs: BuildDynamicFeeCurveDepositPlanInputs,
): Promise<import('@0xintuition/sdk/actions').AgentActionEnvelope>;
```

- **`inputs`**: Chain, contract addresses, the receiver/term/curve to deposit into, and precomputed read values.
- **returns**: An agent-action envelope with the deposit step and the quote it was built from.

## dynamicFeeCurveClaimEnvelope

Builds a batched claim plan for a dynamic-fee curve: settles the caller-supplied
candidate terms and pays out the total claimable across all of them in one `claim`
transaction.

[Source](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/sdk/src/actions/plans/dynamic-fee-curve.ts#L252)

```ts
function dynamicFeeCurveClaimEnvelope(
  inputs: BuildDynamicFeeCurveClaimPlanInputs,
): Promise<import('@0xintuition/sdk/actions').AgentActionEnvelope>;
```

- **`inputs`**: The curve address, the claiming account, and the candidate term IDs to settle.
- **returns**: An agent-action envelope with the claim step and the claimable breakdown it was built from.

### DynamicFeeCurveDepositPlanReadContext

Public export.

```ts
export type DynamicFeeCurveDepositPlanReadContext = {
  curveAddress?: Address;
  config?: DynamicFeeCurvePlanConfig;
  /** Per-tier manual fee override reads, indexed by tier (0-based, matching `config.tierCount`). */
  tierFeeOverrides?: readonly DynamicFeeCurveTierOverrideRead[];
  quoteDepositFee?: bigint;
  previewDeposit?: MultiVaultPreviewDepositResult;
  entryFeeAmount?: bigint;
  protocolFeeAmount?: bigint;
  currentSharePrice?: bigint;
  /** `MultiVault.getVault(termId, curveId).totalShares` — zero means this deposit bootstraps the vault. */
  vaultTotalShares?: bigint;
  /** Only consulted on an empty vault, to double the min-share bootstrap cost for a triple. */
  isTriple?: boolean;
  /** `MultiVault.getGeneralConfig().minShare` — only consulted on an empty vault. */
  minShare?: bigint;
  /** `BondingCurveRegistry.previewMint(minShare, 0, 0, curveId)` — only consulted on an empty vault. */
  previewMint?: bigint;
  /** `totalShares` of the DEFAULT curve's vault, which is what the entry-fee threshold is measured on. */
  defaultVaultTotalShares?: bigint;
  /** `MultiVault.getGeneralConfig().feeThreshold`. Below it the entry fee is waived entirely. */
  feeThreshold?: bigint;
  /** `DynamicFeeFlatPriceCurve.vaultStake(termId)` — what the tier traversal is keyed on. */
  vaultStake?: bigint;
  /** `MultiVault.getGeneralConfig().feeDenominator`, which every MultiVault fee rate is expressed against. */
  feeDenominator?: bigint;
  /** `MultiVault.getAtomConfig().atomWalletDepositFee`, charged on every atom deposit. */
  atomWalletDepositFee?: bigint;
  /** `MultiVault.atomDepositFractionAmount(feeBase)`, charged on a triple deposit. */
  atomDepositFractionAmount?: bigint;
  /** The three atoms under a triple, whose fee thresholds gate the fraction above. */
  tripleAtomIds?: readonly [Hex, Hex, Hex];
};
```

### DynamicFeeCurveClaimPlanReadContext

Public export.

```ts
export type DynamicFeeCurveClaimPlanReadContext = {
  claimableAcross?: bigint;
  /** Per-term pending reads, in the same order as `termIds`. */
  pendingFor?: readonly bigint[];
  /** `DynamicFeeFlatPriceCurve.bankedEarnings(account)` — the settled half of the balance. */
  bankedEarnings?: bigint;
};
```

# FeeProxy action envelopes

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/sdk/plans-fee-proxy

Applies to V2 · `@0xintuition/sdk` 4.0.0

API for `@0xintuition/sdk@4.0.0`. [Compatibility](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/compatibility) · [Source](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/sdk/src/actions/plans/fee-proxy.ts).

Import from `@0xintuition/sdk/actions`.

Signatures show the exact accepted inputs and return types. Named input/output structures and dependency-injection types are listed below; viem and protocol types come from their respective packages. Preparation and quote functions can perform RPC reads. Envelope builders on the action-envelope pages use caller-supplied read context and perform no RPC reads or signing. **`feeProxyExecutePlan` sends transactions**; the other SDK actions on these pages prepare transactions or read data.

## feeProxyCreateAtomsWithUrisEnvelope

Builds a `createAtomsWithUrisVia` plan routed through an affiliate: validates every
atom's URI list against the live URI bounds, quotes the affiliate's creation fee, and
returns the calldata.

[Source](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/sdk/src/actions/plans/fee-proxy.ts#L43)

```ts
function feeProxyCreateAtomsWithUrisEnvelope(
  inputs: BuildFeeProxyCreateAtomsWithUrisPlanInputs,
): Promise<import('@0xintuition/sdk/actions').AgentActionEnvelope>;
```

- **`inputs`**: Chain, contract addresses, the affiliate, per-atom data/assets/URIs, the caller's fee guard, and precomputed read values.
- **returns**: An agent-action envelope with the creation step and the fee/bounds quote it was built from.

# MultiVault action envelopes

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/sdk/plans-multivault

Applies to V2 · `@0xintuition/sdk` 4.0.0

API for `@0xintuition/sdk@4.0.0`. [Compatibility](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/compatibility) · [Source](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/sdk/src/actions/plans/multivault.ts).

Import from `@0xintuition/sdk/actions`.

Signatures show the exact accepted inputs and return types. Named input/output structures and dependency-injection types are listed below; viem and protocol types come from their respective packages. Preparation and quote functions can perform RPC reads. Envelope builders on the action-envelope pages use caller-supplied read context and perform no RPC reads or signing. **`feeProxyExecutePlan` sends transactions**; the other SDK actions on these pages prepare transactions or read data.

## multiVaultDepositEnvelope

Build a JSON-serializable deposit envelope using caller-supplied vault, fee, and preview context. Missing required context throws.

[Source](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/sdk/src/actions/plans/multivault.ts#L200)

```ts
function multiVaultDepositEnvelope(
  inputs: BuildMultiVaultDepositPlanInputs,
): Promise<import('@0xintuition/sdk/actions').AgentActionEnvelope>;
```

## multiVaultRedeemEnvelope

Build a JSON-serializable redemption envelope using caller-supplied balance, fee, and preview context.

[Source](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/sdk/src/actions/plans/multivault.ts#L274)

```ts
function multiVaultRedeemEnvelope(
  inputs: BuildMultiVaultRedeemPlanInputs,
): Promise<import('@0xintuition/sdk/actions').AgentActionEnvelope>;
```

## multiVaultCreateAndSeedEnvelope

Build ordered atom, triple, and seed-deposit steps from explicit creation costs and read context.

[Source](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/sdk/src/actions/plans/multivault.ts#L345)

```ts
function multiVaultCreateAndSeedEnvelope(
  inputs: BuildMultiVaultCreateAndSeedPlanInputs,
): Promise<import('@0xintuition/sdk/actions').AgentActionEnvelope>;
```

## multiVaultOnBehalfOfCreationEnvelope

Builds an on-behalf-of creation plan: `createAtomsFor` / `createTriplesFor` require
`creator` to have granted `caller` CREATION approval first, so this prepends an
`approve` step when the caller reports it isn't granted yet. The approval step and
the creation steps have DIFFERENT required signers (`creator` vs `caller`), surfaced
per-step via `metadata.context.signer` — routing each step to the right signer is the
caller's responsibility.

[Source](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/sdk/src/actions/plans/multivault.ts#L525)

```ts
function multiVaultOnBehalfOfCreationEnvelope(
  inputs: BuildMultiVaultOnBehalfOfCreationPlanInputs,
): Promise<import('@0xintuition/sdk/actions').AgentActionEnvelope>;
```

- **`inputs`**: Chain, MultiVault address, the creator/caller pair, the atoms/triples to create, and the caller's current CREATION/DEPOSIT/REDEMPTION approval state (read live before invoking this plan).
- **returns**: An agent-action envelope with the ordered approval (if needed) and creation steps.

## multiVaultMulticallEnvelope

Builds a consolidated payable `multicall` batch: assembles the `bytes[]` sub-call
array against the aligned `uint256[]` per-sub-call value array, the fiddliest part of
building this call by hand.

[Source](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/sdk/src/actions/plans/multivault.ts#L597)

```ts
function multiVaultMulticallEnvelope(
  inputs: BuildMultiVaultMulticallPlanInputs,
): import('@0xintuition/sdk/actions').AgentActionEnvelope;
```

- **`inputs`**: Chain and the sub-calls to batch, each with its own calldata and value allocation.
- **returns**: An agent-action envelope with the single `multicall` step.

export type BuildMultiVaultOnBehalfOfCreationPlanInputs = {
  chainId?: IntuitionCoreChainId;

  caller: Address;

  triples?: MultiVaultOnBehalfOfTriplePlanInput[];
  approvalAlreadyGranted: boolean;
  /**
   * Whether `creator` already granted `caller` DEPOSIT/REDEMPTION approval. `approve`
   * REPLACES the caller's entire approval bitmask rather than adding a bit, so these
   * must be read live before invoking this plan — omitting them (or defaulting them to
   * `false`) would silently revoke any existing grant the approval step writes over.
   */
  hasDepositApproval: boolean;
  hasRedemptionApproval: boolean;
};

Preparation and quote functions can perform RPC reads. Envelope builders on the action-envelope pages use caller-supplied read context and perform no RPC reads or signing. **`feeProxyExecutePlan` sends transactions**; the other SDK actions on these pages prepare transactions or read data.

## portfolioGetIntuitionPositionsSnapshot

Read balances and vault state for the explicitly supplied account and term/curve positions. This does not discover every position held by an account.

[Source](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/sdk/src/actions/portfolio.ts#L79)

```ts
function portfolioGetIntuitionPositionsSnapshot(
  configs: {
    multiVault: ReadConfig;
    trustBonding: ReadConfig;
  },
  inputs: {
    account: Address;
    positions: PortfolioPositionInput[];
    includeUtilization?: boolean;
    nowTimestamp?: bigint;
  },
  deps?: PortfolioDeps,
): Promise<PortfolioIntuitionPositionsSnapshot>;
```

Defaults: `deps = defaultPortfolioDeps`. Dependency arguments are optional test/customization hooks; normal consumers use the built-in dependencies.

## portfolioGetActionableState

Combine position snapshots with TrustBonding claim state so an application can decide which actions to offer.

[Source](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/sdk/src/actions/portfolio.ts#L128)

```ts
function portfolioGetActionableState(
  configs: {
    multiVault: ReadConfig;
    trustBonding: ReadConfig;
    wrappedTrust?: ReadConfig;
  },
  inputs: {
    account: Address;
    positions: PortfolioPositionInput[];
    nowTimestamp?: bigint;
    recipient?: string | null;
    expectedWrappedTrustSpend?: bigint;
  },
  deps?: PortfolioDeps,
): Promise<PortfolioActionableState>;
```

Defaults: `deps = defaultPortfolioDeps`. Dependency arguments are optional test/customization hooks; normal consumers use the built-in dependencies.

# TrustBonding actions

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/sdk/trust-bonding

Applies to V2 · `@0xintuition/sdk` 4.0.0

API for `@0xintuition/sdk@4.0.0`. [Compatibility](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/compatibility) · [Source](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/sdk/src/actions/trust-bonding.ts).

Import from `@0xintuition/sdk/actions`.

Signatures show the exact accepted inputs and return types. Named input/output structures and dependency-injection types are listed below; viem and protocol types come from their respective packages. Preparation and quote functions can perform RPC reads. Envelope builders on the action-envelope pages use caller-supplied read context and perform no RPC reads or signing. **`feeProxyExecutePlan` sends transactions**; the other SDK actions on these pages prepare transactions or read data.

## trustBondingGetRewardsDashboard

Read epoch, utilization, balance, and reward information for the selected account and return a dashboard snapshot.

[Source](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/sdk/src/actions/trust-bonding.ts#L308)

```ts
function trustBondingGetRewardsDashboard(
  config: ReadConfig,
  inputs: {
    account: Address;
  },
  deps?: TrustBondingDashboardDeps,
): Promise<TrustBondingRewardsDashboard>;
```

Defaults: `deps = defaultTrustBondingDeps`. Dependency arguments are optional test/customization hooks; normal consumers use the built-in dependencies.

## trustBondingGetClaimActionState

Determine whether the selected account can claim rewards and return the reason and claim state for the UI.

[Source](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/sdk/src/actions/trust-bonding.ts#L348)

```ts
function trustBondingGetClaimActionState(
  config: ReadConfig,
  inputs: {
    account: Address;
    recipient?: string | null;
  },
  deps?: TrustBondingDashboardDeps,
): Promise<TrustBondingClaimActionState>;
```

Defaults: `deps = defaultTrustBondingDeps`. Dependency arguments are optional test/customization hooks; normal consumers use the built-in dependencies.

## trustBondingPrepareLockAction

Determine the applicable lock operation and prepare its calldata and value. The result describes the action; it does not request a signature.

[Source](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/sdk/src/actions/trust-bonding.ts#L456)

```ts
function trustBondingPrepareLockAction(
  config: ReadConfig,
  inputs: {
    account: Address;
    amountDelta?: bigint;
    unlockTime?: bigint;
    nowTimestamp?: bigint;
  },
  deps?: TrustBondingLockDeps,
): Promise<TrustBondingLockActionPlan>;
```

Defaults: `deps = defaultTrustBondingLockDeps`. Dependency arguments are optional test/customization hooks; normal consumers use the built-in dependencies.

## trustBondingClaimAndRestakePlan

Prepare ordered claim and restake steps using the current account and lock state. Review the plan before executing it.

[Source](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/sdk/src/actions/trust-bonding.ts#L570)

```ts
function trustBondingClaimAndRestakePlan(
  config: ReadConfig,
  inputs: {
    account: Address;
    recipient?: Address;
    target:
      | {
          kind: 'trust-bonding';
          wrappedTrustAddress: Address;
          beneficiary?: Address;
        }
      | {
          kind: 'multivault';
          receiver?: Address;
          termId: Hex;
          curveId: bigint;
          multiVaultConfig: WriteConfig;
          slippageBps?: bigint;
        };
  },
  deps?: TrustBondingClaimAndRestakeDeps,
): Promise<TrustBondingClaimAndRestakePlanResult>;
```

Defaults: `deps = defaultTrustBondingClaimAndRestakeDeps`. Dependency arguments are optional test/customization hooks; normal consumers use the built-in dependencies.

## trustBondingGetLockStateSummary

Read the account lock balance, expiry, and related state into a normalized summary.

[Source](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/sdk/src/actions/trust-bonding.ts#L695)

```ts
function trustBondingGetLockStateSummary(
  config: ReadConfig,
  inputs: {
    account: Address;
    nowTimestamp?: bigint;
  },
  deps?: TrustBondingLockDeps,
): Promise<TrustBondingLockStateSummary>;
```

Defaults: `deps = defaultTrustBondingLockDeps`. Dependency arguments are optional test/customization hooks; normal consumers use the built-in dependencies.

## trustBondingGetEpochRewardsTimeline

Read reward information across the requested epoch window and return timeline points for presentation.

[Source](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/sdk/src/actions/trust-bonding.ts#L731)

```ts
function trustBondingGetEpochRewardsTimeline(
  config: ReadConfig,
  inputs: {
    account: Address;
    startEpoch: bigint;
    endEpoch: bigint;
  },
  deps?: TrustBondingTimelineDeps,
): Promise<TrustBondingEpochRewardsTimeline>;
```

Defaults: `deps = defaultTrustBondingTimelineDeps`. Dependency arguments are optional test/customization hooks; normal consumers use the built-in dependencies.

## Input and result types

Exported declarations are public imports from the SDK subpath above. Module-local helper aliases describe accepted shapes but are not public exports.

  maxApy?: bigint;
};

  currentEpoch: typeof trustBondingCurrentEpoch;
  userEligibleRewardsForEpoch: typeof trustBondingUserEligibleRewardsForEpoch;
  hasClaimedRewardsForEpoch: typeof trustBondingHasClaimedRewardsForEpoch;
  getUserRewardsForEpoch: typeof trustBondingGetUserRewardsForEpoch;
  getPersonalUtilizationRatio: typeof trustBondingGetPersonalUtilizationRatio;
  getSystemUtilizationRatio: typeof trustBondingGetSystemUtilizationRatio;
};
```
